# Kinetiq — full reference

> A React component library where every animation shares five calibrated springs. Copy the source. Own the code. Ship interfaces that feel machined.

Machine catalog: https://www.kinetiqui.com/registry-meta.json · MCP server: https://www.kinetiqui.com/mcp

## Operating rules (AGENTS.md)

# Kinetiq — Agent Rules

Operating rules for coding agents working with Kinetiq components. Follow
these and anything you compose stays on the system's motion vocabulary.

## The motion language: five calibrated springs

Every animation uses exactly one of five springs from `lib/motion.ts`. Never
hand-write stiffness/damping numbers — reach for a named spring.

| Spring | stiffness / damping / mass | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flick` | 1100 / 55 / 0.7 | Press states, tick draws, focus. **Confirms.** |
| `snap` | 640 / 42 / 1.0 | Toggles, tab indicators, menus. One crisp overshoot. **Switches.** |
| `glide` | 300 / 34 / 1.0 | Layout shifts, reorders, morphs. **Moves.** |
| `drift` | 120 / 24 / 1.2 | Large surfaces, ambient motion, parallax settle. **Breathes.** |
| `recoil` | 520 / 24 / 1.0 | Toasts, stamps, landings. Two visible bounces. **Celebrates.** |

Say the verb the interaction performs — confirm, switch, move, breathe,
celebrate — and you have the spring.

## Tweens, not springs, for surface properties

Springs drive spatial change (position, scale, rotation). Opacity, color,
blur, and clip use the tween scale from `lib/motion.ts`:

- Durations: `blink 0.08` · `fast 0.15` · `base 0.24` · `slow 0.40` · `page 0.70`
- Easings: `enter [0.22,1,0.36,1]` · `exit [0.5,0,0.75,0]` · `move [0.65,0,0.35,1]` · `linear`
- Enter offsets: `nudge 4` · `step 8` · `shift 16` (px). Scale-ins start at 0.96, never 0.

## Orchestration

- **600ms budget.** A choreographed sequence never exceeds 600ms total. Use
  `cascade(count)` for the stagger interval — it tightens automatically as the
  count grows.
- **Exits are tweens at 0.6x the enter duration** with the `exit` easing, via
  `exitFor()`. Never spring an exit — it reads as indecision.
- One spatial axis per element; stagger from the element the user touched.

## Reduced motion is a first-class state

Read `useMotionSafe()` — never call `matchMedia` directly. When it returns
false, degrade, do not disable:

- Transform enters → opacity fade at `fast`.
- Discrete springs → instant position + a color tween.
- Direct manipulation (drag, sliders) → keep 1:1 tracking; drop inertia and settle.
- Autoplay loops → static (marquees become a wrapped grid).
- Scroll-linked → final state, opacity only. Number rolls → instant value + highlight.

## Tokens

Use shadcn semantic tokens only: `bg-background/card/popover/primary/muted/accent/destructive`,
`text-*-foreground`, `border-border/input`, `ring`. For live-data accents
(readouts, traces, LIVE badges) use `var(--signal, var(--primary))`. Radii:
`rounded-1` (2px) · `rounded-2` (6px) · `rounded-3` (10px) · `rounded-4` (16px).

## Accessibility

Every interactive component ships real WAI-ARIA roles, complete keyboard
support, and visible focus rings (`:focus-visible`, never removed). Silent
state changes announce through an sr-only live region.

## Installing

Components are distributed as source through a shadcn-compatible registry.

```sh
# One-time: register the namespace
npx shadcn@latest registry add @kinetiq=https://www.kinetiqui.com/r/{name}.json
# Then add by name
npx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pressure-button
# Or zero-config by URL
npx shadcn@latest add https://www.kinetiqui.com/r/pressure-button.json
```

Installed components import shared helpers (`lib/motion`, `lib/utils`, the
`use-motion-safe` hook) via your project's aliases — the CLI rewrites them on
install. Don't edit those shared files per-component; they're the shared
vocabulary.

## Motion system

Five calibrated springs — every animation uses one of them:

- `springs.flick` — stiffness 1100, damping 55, mass 0.7 (ζ 0.99, settles ~120ms). Press states, tick draws, focus. Confirms.
- `springs.snap` — stiffness 640, damping 42, mass 1 (ζ 0.83, settles ~300ms). Toggles, tab indicators, menus — one crisp overshoot. Switches.
- `springs.glide` — stiffness 300, damping 34, mass 1 (ζ 0.98, settles ~450ms). Layout shifts, reorders, morphs. Moves.
- `springs.drift` — stiffness 120, damping 24, mass 1.2 (ζ 1, settles ~800ms). Large surfaces, ambient drift, parallax settle. Breathes.
- `springs.recoil` — stiffness 520, damping 24, mass 1 (ζ 0.53, settles ~700ms). Toasts, stamps, landings — two visible bounces. Celebrates.

Cascade: Stagger interval = clamp(0.6 / (count - 1), 0.02, 0.06)s so the whole choreography stays under a 600ms budget; dense lists tighten automatically.
Exits: Exits are always tweens at 0.6x the enter duration with the exit easing — springs on exit read as indecision.
Reduced motion: prefers-reduced-motion is a first-class state. Transform enters become opacity fades; discrete springs snap to position with a color tween; direct manipulation keeps 1:1 tracking but drops inertia; autoplay loops go static; scroll-linked renders its final frame; number rolls swap instantly. Every component reads useMotionSafe(), never matchMedia directly.

## Catalog

### Pressure Button (KQ-001) — `pressure-button`
A button that pushes back.

A button that pushes back — press squash on flick, spring rebound on snap, and a hold-to-confirm gauge ring for destructive actions.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pressure-button`

Props:
- `variant`: "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "danger" (default "solid") — Visual style. Danger pairs naturally with holdToConfirm.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Control height and typography scale.
- `holdToConfirm`: number — Milliseconds the button must be held before confirming. Adds a gauge ring; Escape or early release cancels.
- `onConfirm`: () => void — Fires when a hold completes. Hold buttons never fire onClick.

Notes:
- Space and Enter drive the same physics as the pointer — hold either to confirm.
- Under reduced motion the squash is replaced by a shade change; the gauge ring still fills because progress is feedback, not flourish.

### Trace Input (KQ-002) — `trace-input`
Focus draws its own boundary.

A plain text field with the focus drawn rather than switched on. A stroke traces the field's perimeter as it takes focus and the label warms to the ring colour; errors nudge the box and annotate themselves with a dimension line. The label sits above the box, so the affixes and the text share one centred line inside it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/trace-input`

Props:
- `label`: string — Field label, rendered above the box. Pass labelHidden to keep it for assistive tech only.
- `description / error`: string — Helper and error lines below the field, chained into aria-describedby. Errors nudge the field and set aria-invalid.
- `prefix / suffix`: ReactNode — Leading and trailing slots inside the field.
- `…input props`: Omit<InputProps, "prefix"> — Standard input passthrough; controlled and uncontrolled both work.

Notes:
- The perimeter trace doubles as the focus indicator — it is never removed, only accelerated.
- The label is above the box, so pass a placeholder for hint text inside it; nothing is reserved and every child stays centred.
- Under reduced motion the stroke appears instantly and the error nudge is skipped; the message still announces via aria-invalid.

### Breaker Switch (KQ-003) — `breaker-switch`
A toggle with mechanical conviction.

A toggle with mechanical conviction — the thumb stretches in anticipation while held, throws on snap, and squashes against the track end as the rail recoils.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/breaker-switch`

Props:
- `checked / defaultChecked / onCheckedChange`: boolean / boolean / (checked) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled state.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Fixed geometry — travel is derived, nothing is measured.
- `onLabel / offLabel`: string — Tiny uppercase text inside the track ends.
- `label`: ReactNode — Adjacent clickable label, associated automatically.
- `name / value`: string — Renders a hidden input that submits while checked.

Notes:
- A native button with role="switch" — Space and Enter throw it, and Space arms the anticipation stretch.
- Under reduced motion the thumb repositions instantly; only the color crossfade remains.

### Checkbox (KQ-004) — `checkbox`
The tick is drawn, not shown.

The tick is drawn, not shown — a pathLength stroke on flick, an indeterminate dash that slides in, and group select-alls that cascade down the list.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/checkbox`

Props:
- `checked / defaultChecked`: boolean — Controlled or uncontrolled checked state.
- `indeterminate`: boolean (default false) — Mixed state — dash visual plus native el.indeterminate.
- `onCheckedChange`: (checked: boolean) => void — Fires with the next checked state.
- `label / description`: ReactNode — Visible label (required) and muted secondary line.
- `CheckboxGroup`: items, value, onValueChange, selectAll, legend… — Fieldset-based group with select-all parent (checked / unchecked / indeterminate) and cascading tick draws.

Notes:
- Native hidden inputs do the accessibility work; the drawn box is decorative.
- Under reduced motion ticks appear instantly and select-all cascades lose their stagger.

### Caliper Slider (KQ-005) — `caliper-slider`
Reads like a vernier, moves like grease.

Reads like a vernier, moves like grease — 1:1 drag with a snap settle, ticks that lean toward the jaw, and a live measured-span dimension line in range mode.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/caliper-slider`

Props:
- `min / max / step`: number (default 0 / 100 / 1) — Bounds and snap grid (float-precision cleaned).
- `value / defaultValue / onValueChange`: number | [number, number] — Single or range; live stepped values during drag, deduped.
- `range`: boolean (default false) — Two facing caliper jaws with a live span dimension line.
- `marks`: number[] | boolean (default true) — Every step when ≤ 40 steps, else quarters; or pinned positions.
- `format / readout`: (v) => string / "float" | "end" | "none" — Value formatting and where the mono readout renders.

Notes:
- Full APG slider keyboard set per thumb; range thumbs cross-clamp their ARIA bounds.
- Under reduced motion tracking stays 1:1 — only the tick lean and the settle spring are removed.

### Gantry Tabs (KQ-006) — `gantry-tabs`

Notes:

- Under reduced motion drawers open instantly and content crossfades — no lag, no sibling nudge.

### Callout (KQ-008) — `callout`

Notes:

### Telemetry Toast (KQ-011) — `telemetry-toast`

Notes:

### Tool Trace (KQ-218) — `tool-trace`
The run at chip height.

A tool run folded into a chip: collapsed, one line says what happened — 4 tool calls, 2 messages — and open, the run replays as its parts: a thinking note, a code write on the lathe, a command with its checks printing, a read with what was seen. File-change chips close the run with +/− counts and an honest overflow. The point is proportion: agents work loudly, and a transcript that prints every tool call at full height buries the answer the run was for.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tool-trace`

- `calls`: ToolCall[] — Thinking, write, run, and read parts, in order.
- `changes / maxChanges`: FileChange[] · number — File chips with +/− counts; the rest fold into +N more.
- `summary / defaultOpen`: string · boolean — The collapsed line, and whether the run starts open.

Notes:
- The code write composes code-lathe (whole, diff gutters on), so the snippet is copyable and complete for assistive tech from first paint.
- Collapsed is the honest default — the answer matters more than the machinery that fetched it.
- The overflow count is real: chips beyond maxChanges are counted, never dropped silently.

A button that plays hard to get exactly twice, then relents — approach it with a pointer and it springs to the next seat in a fixed cycle, and after two dodges it returns to centre and lets you click it. Keyboard users are never dodged, and neither are touch devices, because a button that runs away from a thumb is not a joke, it is a bug.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/dodge-button`

Props:
- `label`: string (default "Delete everything") — What the button claims it will do.
- `dodges`: number (default 2) — Evasions before it relents (0–4).

Notes:
- Keyboard focus and Enter or Space never trigger a dodge — the bit is pointer-only, by design.
- Coarse pointers are exempt entirely; the button simply works on touch.
- Reduced motion skips the bit and presents a normal button from the start.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/focus-rail`

Props:
- `items`: FocusRailItem[] — Panels in order; each carries an id, a label, and optional detail content.
- `activeId`: string — Controlled active panel; omit to let the rail manage it.
- `grow`: number (default 2.4) — Flex weight of the expanded panel.
- `expandOn`: "hover" | "press" (default "hover") — Whether hovering expands, or only a press.

Notes:
- Galleries and team sections compose this rather than re-deriving the flex spring.
- Focus always expands the focused panel regardless of mode — keyboard intent is intent.
- Reduced motion resizes panels instantly and swaps detail without fades.

### Turn Modal (KQ-349) — `turn-modal`
Two faces of one object.

A card that lifts, travels to the centre, and turns over on Y into a focus-trapped dialog — the flip and the travel are one motion, so the dialog face comes around mid-flight and is never visible early. - Reduced motion drops the flight and the turn; the dialog fades in centred with the trap intact.

Display text whose glyphs compress under the cursor and rebound when it leaves — each letter its own spring, so a word behaves like a row of rubber blocks. - Reduced motion renders the text plainly with no deformation.

### Mask Field (KQ-491) — `mask-field`
The format arrives as you type.

A text field that wears its format. Ghost glyphs hold the shape of what is expected, and as characters land the mask's separators arrive on flick — scaling up from 0.6 as the ink comes in — while deleting pulls them back out the same way. One real input carries the value beneath a transparent text layer so a monospace cell grid can draw the glyphs, which keeps the native keyboard intact: typing, backspace across a separator, selection and paste all behave as the browser intends, and a pasted number fills every slot in a single cascade inside the 600ms budget.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mask-field`

Props:
- `mask`: string — The shape, with # for a digit and A for a letter, e.g. "(###) ###-####" or "#### #### #### ####".
- `value / defaultValue`: string — Raw characters, without separators — controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (raw: string, formatted: string) => void — Both readings on every change.
- `label`: string — Visible label above the box.
- `placeholderChar`: string (default "_") — The ghost glyph standing in for an empty slot.

Notes:
- The keyboard is the browser's own: typing, paste, undo and selection are native, and backspace deletes the character a separator stands in front of rather than stalling on the separator.
- Under reduced motion the ink still changes and the separators still arrive — only the scale and the 4px drop are dropped.
- The drawn glyph layer is aria-hidden; the single real input carries the accessible value, so form posts, autofill and screen readers see the formatted string.

### Typeahead Field (KQ-492) — `typeahead-field`
The rest of the word arrives in grey.

A field that finishes the word for you. The best match's remainder sits in grey just past the caret, and accepting it wipes the grey copy left to right over durations.base to reveal the committed ink underneath, so the completion is seen becoming real rather than swapped for real. Beneath, matches cascade() in with the typed span emphasised and a single marker rides between them on snap, carried by one layoutId; the input never loses focus, so ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the marker, Tab or ArrowRight takes the completion, Enter picks the marked row and Escape closes the list.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/typeahead-field`

Props:
- `suggestions`: string[] — The vocabulary to complete from; prefix matches are ranked above matches found inside the word.
- `value / defaultValue`: string — The typed text — controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires on typing and on accept.
- `onAccept`: (value: string) => void — Fires when a suggestion is accepted, by completion or by pick.
- `maxItems`: number (default 6) — Suggestions shown under the field.
- `label`: string — Visible label above the box.

Notes:
- Tab or ArrowRight (with the caret at the end) accepts the completion, ArrowDown opens the list and steps the marker, ArrowUp steps back, Enter picks the marked row, Escape closes. Tab only holds the field while a completion is offered — once accepted, the next Tab leaves.
- Under reduced motion the list appears without the cascade, the marker jumps between rows, and the completion commits without the sweep; the matches and the emphasis are unchanged.
- Combobox semantics throughout: focus and the caret stay in the input while aria-activedescendant points at the marked option, and the panel is measured with a ResizeObserver so it animates when the match count changes rather than reserving room.

### Strength Field (KQ-493) — `strength-field`

A password field that shows its work. ### Catch Zone (KQ-494) — `catch-zone`

- Rejections carry the reason in a role=alert line and never animate approvingly; the drag counter tolerates enter and leave events from child elements, so the frame does not flicker as the pointer crosses the caption.

### Signature Pad (KQ-495) — `signature-pad`
Ink that remembers the pen's speed.

An SVG pad whose ink remembers the pen. Each sample's nib width comes from the speed since the last one, smoothed so the line eases rather than flickers — a fast flourish thins, a slow stop pools — and every stroke is a filled ribbon revealed through a mask that runs along the pen's own path. That is what lets Clear rewind instead of blink: each stroke un-writes on glide, last one first, cascade() apart, while Undo lifts a single stroke away on a fade. - `onTypedChange`: (typed: string) => void — Fires with the typed-signature fallback's text, so a form can accept either way of signing.
- `penColor`: string (default "currentColor") — CSS colour for the ink; inherits the pad's text colour by default, so it reads in both themes.
- `height`: number (default 160) — Pad height in px; the width fills the container.
- `label`: string — Caption above the pad; it names the whole group, controls included.
- `allowTyped`: boolean (default true) — Offers the typed-signature fallback below the pad.

Notes:
- Drawing is pointer-only by nature, so the keyboard path is a typed signature: a real text input, labelled and described as an equal way to sign rather than a consolation. Undo and Clear are ordinary buttons, reachable by Tab and fired by Space or Enter, and disabled when there is nothing to take back.
- Under reduced motion Clear and Undo are instant — no rewind, no lift — while the ink itself, its taper included, is unchanged.
- The pad claims pointer capture only after 4px of travel, so a plain tap is never swallowed, and a stroke that leaves the pad mid-flourish still finishes.

- `unit / defaultUnit`: 0 | 1 (default 0) — Controlled or initial unit index.
- `onUnitChange`: (index: 0 | 1) => void — Fires on flip with the index now showing.
- `label`: React.ReactNode — What is being measured; sits opposite the readout and truncates rather than wrapping.

Notes:

- `className`: string — Outer classes. Padding belongs on the content, not on the panel.

Notes:

### Path Rider (KQ-575) — `path-rider`
It rides the path as you scroll.

Something that rides a path. One value between zero and one places the rider at that fraction of the path's length using the browser's own geometry — a point plus the two either side of it, which give the tangent it turns to — and the travelled part of the route draws in behind it from the same value through pathLength, so the line and the rider cannot disagree. - `container`: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> — Scroll-link source; used when progress is omitted.
- `rider`: React.ReactNode — What travels. Defaults to a chevron badge.
- `playing`: boolean (default false) — Runs progress to the end on a linear tween.
- `duration`: number (default 4000) — Length of a full run, ms.
- `onProgressChange`: (progress: number) => void — Fires with progress, 0–1, whenever the whole percent changes.
- `onPlayEnd`: () => void — Fires when a run reaches the end.
- `label`: string (default Route) — Names the route in the caption.

Notes:
- The rider is decorative and aria-hidden; position is exposed as text in the caption, so drive it from a control that carries its own semantics — a native range input, or the container's scroll.
- Progress has one source at a time: playing wins, then a controlled progress prop, then the container's scroll. Scroll mapping is linear on purpose — a spring on a scroll-linked value lags the finger.
- Under reduced motion a run advances in eight jumps instead of gliding, so the trip still finishes and still reports; scrubbed and scroll-linked progress place the rider without travel either way.

### Scroll Frames (KQ-580) — `scroll-frames`
Scroll scrubs the sequence.

A frame sequence scrubbed by scroll. The stage pins to the top of its container while a tall spacer scrolls past underneath, and the fraction already gone picks the frame — linearly, because a scrub has no physics of its own and any easing laid over it would fight the finger. Frames are drawn rather than loaded: renderFrame is handed a context already scaled to the display and sized by a ResizeObserver, and the sequence redraws itself when the box or the theme changes.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/scroll-frames`

Props:
- `frames`: number — Frame count. The last frame owns the final sliver, so a fully scrolled stage lands on the end.
- `renderFrame`: (index: number, ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, size: { w: number; h: number }) => void — Draws one frame in logical pixels; the retina scale and the clear are already done.
- `container`: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> — The scrolling element the stage is pinned inside — never the window.
- `height`: number (default 600) — Scroll distance the sequence is spread over. Minus the container's height, this is the scrub.
- `label`: string (default "Frame sequence") — Names the canvas, which is exposed as an image.
- `onFrameChange`: (index: number) => void — Fires with the frame index whenever it changes, from scroll and from the reduced-motion scrubber alike.

Notes:
- Scrolling is the container's own, so give that container tabIndex 0 and a name: arrows, Page keys and Home/End then scrub the sequence with no extra key handling.
- Under reduced motion nothing is pinned and nothing moves on its own — the stage shows the final frame at its natural height with a native range input under it, so the whole sequence can still be read.
- Keep renderFrame referentially stable (useCallback) and pure: it is called on every frame change, resize and theme flip, and reading tokens off ctx.canvas keeps the drawing correct in both themes.

- `format`: (value: number) => string (default Intl.NumberFormat, two decimals) — Formats the amount.
- `labels`: Partial<Record<SettleStatus, string>> (default Pending / Settled / Returned) — Overrides the word for any state.
- `network`: string — Who has to say so — printed under the pill and named in the announcement.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" (default md) — Pill height: h-7 or h-9, so it keeps the row height it sits in.
- `onSettled`: (status: SettleStatus) => void — Fires once the stamp has landed, from the animation's own completion.

Notes:
- A polite role="status" carrying a whole sentence for assistive technology, so the state is never colour or pulse alone. It is a readout with no interactive parts, so it never takes focus.
- The pill's width is measured from its content with a ResizeObserver rather than guessed, so a longer word widens it exactly.
- Under reduced motion there is no breath and no halo, the widening is instant, and the tick appears already drawn.

- `size`: "sm" | "md" (default "md") — The 24px row badge or the 28px card badge; both keep one radius.
- `name`: string — What the badge is about ("Invoice 4821"), spoken before the state.
- `announce`: boolean (default true) — Keeps the polite live region that reads the new state once it settles.

Notes:
- Colour never carries the state alone: each state has its own glyph and its own words, and the pill's visuals are hidden from assistive technology so the standing arrives as one sentence rather than three fragments.
- Under reduced motion nothing pulses, wipes or recoils — the colour transitions, the label cross-fades in place and the tick appears already drawn.
- A display control with no pointer gesture: it is not focusable and owes no keyboard path; drive it from the state that owns the invoice.

### Retry Schedule (KQ-683) — `retry-schedule`
When we will try again.

A failed charge and the plan for trying it again: spent attempts are struck dots, the next one is ringed and breathing on drift, and the connector into it is the countdown made visible, filling at a linear rate while the mm:ss beside it ticks from an interval that stops when the tab is hidden and holds while an attempt is in flight. Retry now fires the attempt early from the press, and a settled attempt lands — a failure strikes its dot on flick, a success draws its tick on flick and lands the dot on recoil, the one place two bounces are earned. The schedule is an ordered list whose items carry sentences, so the drawn rail stays decorative and the countdown sits in an aria-live="off" timer that is queried rather than announced every second.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/retry-schedule`

- `reason / method`: string (default "Card declined") — The decline line and the quiet caption naming the method that failed.
- `running`: boolean (default true) — Runs the countdown. It also stops while the document is hidden or while busy.
- `busy`: boolean (default false) — The attempt is in flight: the button reads Trying, its ring spins, and the countdown holds.
- `onRetryNow`: () => void — Fires from the press on Retry now.
- `onElapse`: () => void — Fires from the interval when the wait reaches zero, so the host can run the attempt.
- `onTick`: (secondsLeft: number) => void — Fires once a second from the interval with the seconds left.
- `label`: string (default "Retry schedule") — Names the schedule for assistive technology.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion nothing breathes, spins or recoils — the connector still fills and the tick appears already drawn, because a countdown and an outcome are information.

### Rate Ladder (KQ-717) — `rate-ladder`
Longer terms, higher rungs.

A ladder of term deposits: two stiles with a rung per term, the shortest at the bottom and the longest at the top, so higher rungs pay more. Picking a rung lifts it off the stiles on snap — two pixels up, a raised surface and a cobalt edge, one crisp overshoot — while the rung it replaces settles back, and on the same beat the headline rate rolls its digits and, given a principal, the interest at maturity rolls beside it. - `label`: string — Names the ladder; printed as the heading and read as the radio group's label.

Notes:
- A radio group under the hood: Tab lands on the chosen rung, Up and Right step to a longer term and Down and Left to a shorter one without wrapping, Home is the shortest and End the longest, arrows select as they move, and Space or Enter select the focused rung. Each rung is named by its sentence and the readout is a status line, so a pick is announced once.
- Under reduced motion the chosen rung changes colour and edge only, the rate and interest swap their digits in place, and the marker and track fill jump on a fast tween — which rung is chosen still shows.
- Pass start as a fixed date rather than today's: the ladder never reads a clock, so server and client render the same maturities.

Notes:

- `words`: VoiceWord[] (default []) — { id, text, final } — interim words read light, final words firm to full ink.
- `holding`: boolean — Optional controlled hold state; the component holds its own when omitted.
- `onHoldStart`: () => void — Fires from the press that begins a hold; start listening here.
- `onSend`: (text: string) => void — Fires from the release with the joined words.
- `onCancel`: () => void — Fires from Escape during a hold, a lost focus, or a release with nothing said.
- `label`: string (default "Hold to talk") — The button's accessible name.

Notes:
- Hold Space or Enter to talk and release to send; Escape cancels; the button carries aria-pressed for the hold and a description of the gesture, the transcript is a plain paragraph, and a status line announces the hold, the send and a cancel — never a word as it arrives.
- Under reduced motion the rings hold their size and show the level as wash opacity, words appear in place and firm by colour, and the stamp fades in.
- The parent owns the audio: begin listening in onHoldStart, feed level and words as they arrive, and clear them in onSend — nothing in the component touches a microphone or a clock.

### Context Chips (KQ-756) — `context-chips`
What the model can see.

What the model can see, as a strip of chips at the head of a composer: one per context item with a glyph for its kind, its name and its size. Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/context-chips`

- `format`: (bytes: number) => string (default formatSize) — Formats every size; the default prints B, KB or MB.
- `label`: string — Names the strip as a group.

Notes:

- The parent owns the items: add them as the user attaches context and drop them in onRemove; the strip animates whatever the array does and prints the total against the budget.

### Prompt History (KQ-757) — `prompt-history`

- `label`: string — Names the field.

The lock's shackle closes on flick, turning the field read-only and settling the regenerate control's randomness dots to one faint grey; unlocking opens the shackle and rolls a new seed at once, derived from the old one by an integer hash so server and client agree. Typing edits the seed directly.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/seed-lock`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "48213907") — Controlled or initial seed, digits only.
- `onValueChange`: (seed: string, reason: "typed" | "rolled") => void — Fires from a keystroke, an unlock or the regenerate control.
- `locked / defaultLocked`: boolean (default false) — Controlled or initial lock state.
- `onLockedChange`: (locked: boolean) => void — Fires from the lock switch.
- `maxDigits`: number (default 9) — Longest seed the field accepts.
- `label`: string — Names the field.

Notes:
- The input is a numeric text field labelled by label, read-only while locked; the lock is a switch named "Lock seed" and the regenerate control a button named "New seed" that stays focusable while disabled so the keyboard can read why.
- Under reduced motion the digits swap in place, the shackle swaps open or closed and the dots swap their pattern — the read-only dim still shows.
- The status region speaks from the lock and the roll only, never from a keystroke; nextSeed is exported so a host can derive the same roll.

### Sampling Graph (KQ-790) — `sampling-graph`
Where the next word comes from.

A bar chart of next-token probabilities drawn from the host's logits by a softmax at the given temperature, a repetition penalty on tokens already seen and a top-p nucleus that cuts the tail. Rows are keyed by token and sorted by probability, so a parameter change that reorders them is a FLIP layout move on glide while each bar scales on glide and the percentages roll on snap. A seeded draw picks one token and its bar lights: the fill turns signal and a pip lands on flick; a settle timer speaks the pick once the parameters are still.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sampling-graph`

Props:
- `candidates`: SamplingCandidate[] — { token, logit, seen? }; at most a dozen rows read well.
- `temperature`: number (default 1) — Softmax temperature; clamped to 0.05 or more.
- `penalty`: number (default 1) — Repetition penalty dividing the logit of seen tokens; 1 is off.
- `topP`: number (default 1) — Nucleus share; tokens past it are cut and never drawn.
- `seed`: number (default 1) — Seeds the draw that picks the token.
- `onSettle`: (pick: SamplingPick) => void — Fires from the settle timer with { token, probability, rank } once the parameters have been still for half a second.
- `label`: string — Names the chart.

Notes:
- The chart takes no input: every parameter is a prop the host's own controls drive, so the keyboard path is the host's; rows are list items carrying the token, its percentage, "cut" and "picked" as text.
- Under reduced motion rows swap into their new order without travelling, bars tween, digits swap and the pick's light is a colour swap — the sort and the light still happen, because they are information.
- sampleDistribution is exported so a host can read the same pick the chart shows without waiting for the settle; every probability is rounded to six decimals and every width to three before it reaches an attribute.

### Plan Tree (KQ-791) — `plan-tree`
The task, broken down.

A tree of steps that unfolds while an agent plans. Rows arrive from a nudge on the enter ease and a branch's group grows to a measured height on glide as sub-steps are planned; a running node breathes, a done node fills and ticks on flick, a failed one crosses in danger. Bumping a branch's plan revision folds it on the exit ease and regrows it on glide with a cascade. Arrow keys walk the tree, Right opens or enters a branch, Left folds or leaves it, Enter and Space toggle.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/plan-tree`

Props:
- `nodes`: PlanNode[] — The plan, root steps in order; append to unfold it. A node with a children array is a branch, and its plan revision re-plans it when bumped.
- `expanded / defaultExpanded`: string[] — Controlled or initial open branches; omitted, every branch starts open.
- `onExpandedChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — Fires from a row press or an arrow key with every open branch id.
- `label`: string — Names the tree.

Notes:
- A role=tree with a roving tabindex: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move, ArrowRight opens a branch or enters it, ArrowLeft folds it or moves to the parent, Home and End jump, Enter and Space toggle; a row press toggles too.
- Under reduced motion rows appear in place on an opacity tween, the running node holds at mid opacity, marks are drawn whole, and group heights change on a tween.
- The live region speaks the running step's path, a failure, a re-plan, and completion once per change, never per tick.

- `runLabels`: [string, string] (default ["Previous", "Current"]) — Names the two runs in the legend and the row sentences.
- `onSettle`: (regressions: number) => void — Fires from the beat's timer when the sorted order lands, with the regression count.
- `label`: string — Names the list for assistive technology.

Notes:

- `stampText`: string (default "Reviewed") — The word on the seal.
- `label`: string — Names the card for assistive technology.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion the seal fades in and out at rest — no drop, no tilt landing, no peel — and the tooltip fades without scaling; the success tint still tweens.

### Risk Meter (KQ-839) — `risk-meter`

A meter beneath a proposed action that fills toward its risk: the fill is a scaleX on glide, toned cobalt, warn or danger by band, with two threshold ticks on the track, and a band label rides above it with its centre on the fill's leading edge while its word rolls up or down on snap. - `messages`: PreviewMessage[] — The thread, oldest first: id, from (me or peer), optional text, attachments and time.

- `onSend`: (draft: { text: string; attachments: Attachment[] }) => void — Fires from Enter or Send; clear pending and append the message in the same commit so the thumbnails fly.
- `peerName`: string (default "Them") — Names the other side in the composer's label and the thread's sentences.
- `placeholder`: string (default "Message") — The textarea's placeholder.
- `label`: string — Names the thread list for assistive technology.

Notes:
- The thread is an ordered list whose own items read "You sent 2 attachments: pallet-a.jpg, pallet-b.jpg"; the strip is a labelled list of images named by kind and file, each with a named remove button, and focus moves to the next remove control or back to Attach as the strip empties.
- The composer is a real textarea: Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks a line, and Send is disabled while there is neither text nor a pending file.
- Under reduced motion nothing flies and nothing rises — thumbnails fade in place — but the slots and the strip still open and close on fast tweens, because a slot collapsing is feedback rather than flourish.

The card rotates about its horizontal axis on snap — one crisp overshoot, two keyframes — with the original and the translation as the two faces of one card, each hiding its back, while observers measure both faces so the card glides to the active one's height on glide rather than reserving room for the longer text. The original stays under a fold that opens at a measured height, Escape closes it and hands focus back, and a language chip rides the corner rail from one corner to the other as a layout FLIP.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/translate-flip`

Props:
- `text`: string — The message as it arrived, in the source language.
- `translation`: string — The rendering in the reader's language.
- `source / target`: TranslateLanguage — Where it came from and the reader's language; each is a code for the chip and a name for every control.
- `translated / defaultTranslated`: boolean (default false) — Controlled or initial face.
- `onTranslatedChange`: (translated: boolean) => void — Fires from the control or Space with the next face.
- `originalOpen / defaultOriginalOpen`: boolean (default false) — Controlled or initial state of the fold that holds the original.
- `onOriginalOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the fold control, from Escape, and when turning back closes the fold.
- `pending`: boolean (default false) — The host is still producing the translation: the chip turns an arc and the control refuses with aria-disabled.
- `author`: string — Printed above the card.
- `time`: string — Sent time, already formatted.
- `label`: string (default "Thread") — Names the thread list for assistive technology.

Notes:
- Translate is an aria-pressed button named for the language it will show; the fold is aria-expanded and aria-controls its region, and Escape anywhere in the card closes the fold and returns focus to the fold control.
- Both faces stay in the DOM and the one that is turned away is aria-hidden and inert to the pointer, so a screen reader never reads the same message twice.
- Under reduced motion the card does not turn: the faces cross-fade in place, the chip swaps corners at once and the pending arc holds still, while the measured height still changes because which language you are reading is information.

### Presence Dot (KQ-871) — `presence-dot`

Four states drawn as four shapes, so colour is never the only signal: online fills, away takes a crescent bite, busy is crossed by a bar, offline is a hollow dimmed ring. The bite and the bar are holes in one SVG mask that scale in on snap, away breathes a slow mirrored ring, and every change rings once from a key rather than a timer. - `name`: string — Whose presence it is; opens the spoken sentence.

- `detail`: string — A quieter trailing clause ("back at 15:30"), spoken with the status.

- `showWord`: boolean (default true) — Draws the status word beside the mark, so the shape is never alone.
- `ring`: boolean (default true) — The one-shot ring on a change; turn it off in dense rosters.
- `onAnnounce`: (sentence: string) => void — Fires from an effect once per frozen sentence, after a change.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion the shapes still swap and offline still dims — shape is information — but nothing breathes, rings or scales.

- `className`: string — Classes for the outer column.

Notes:
- Each sticker is a button named with a sentence ("Replay sticker: cat, from Marta") and the drawing inside is aria-hidden, so the picture is never read as a glyph; Enter and Space replay, and focus draws the same nudge hovering does.
- Under reduced motion nothing drops and nothing tilts — the sticker fades in at rest — but a press is still answered by a ring that pulses once, because the acknowledgement is information even when the bounce is not.
- Arrivals announce themselves once from a sentence frozen at the change, so a parent re-render never re-announces a sticker that landed long ago.

### GIF Loop (KQ-886) — `gif-loop`

Notes:

### Audio Wave (KQ-887) — `audio-wave`

- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Holds every field and control.
- `className`: string — Extra classes on the card.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion the two faces cross-fade on a fast tween, the summary rows arrive together instead of cascading, and the Sent chip appears at full size with no bounce.

- Each row is a disclosure button with aria-expanded that names itself as one sentence — probe, target and how it went — under a roving tabindex: Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space folds or unfolds.
- An uncontrolled list opens a check the moment it settles to fail, because a failed check must not stay shut; a controlled host keeps its own set and should open the failed id itself from onOpenChange or its own state.
- A failure and the final tally are announced once through a polite live region, and the settled rule is a role="meter" whose value text is a sentence.
- Under reduced motion the ring holds still while the row still prints running, and ticks and crosses appear at full size, because a settled check is information.

### Rollback Arc (KQ-969) — `rollback-arc`
Back to the last good one.

Every version a service has worn, laid on one static arc with the newest at the frontier and each node's coordinates rounded before they reach an attribute. The deployed marker rides the curve rather than cutting the chord: one scalar motion value carries its position between version indices and useTransform derives cx and cy from it, so a rollback across three versions travels the arc on glide. Choosing an earlier node moves a hollow caret to it on snap and unfolds a roll-back row at a ResizeObserver-measured height, and only when the marker has settled does the version become current and the sentence get spoken.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/rollback-arc`

- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the frontier) — Controlled or initial deployed version id.

- `onChosenChange`: (id: string) => void — The caret's version — a state, so it also fires on the first commit.
- `onRollbackStart`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the press that started the travel.
- `rollbackLabel`: (version: ReleaseVersion) => string (default "Roll back to <label>" or "Roll forward to <label>") — Copy on the confirm control; the default names the direction.

- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:

- The confirm button is focused as its row arrives and uses aria-disabled while the marker travels, so it never drops the keyboard mid-press; onValueChange fires only once the marker has settled, so drive the real rollback from onRollbackStart and treat onValueChange as done.
- Under reduced motion the marker does not travel — it jumps and the arrival is spoken at once — because where the service now stands is information.

### Queue Depth (KQ-970) — `queue-depth`
Waiting to deploy.

What is waiting to go out, in the order it will go: the head carries a rule that drains on glide to its share of the seconds left, and a Hold switch stops it, because a queue you cannot stop is not a queue. Pressing a row promotes it one place and the two neighbours exchange under layout on glide, a FLIP rather than a re-render; two adjacent rows for the same service can be merged, the lower leaving on a fast exit while the upper takes its changes and its count cross-fades in one grid cell. Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/queue-depth`

- `held / defaultHeld`: boolean (default false) — Controlled or initial hold on the head of the queue.

- `onQueueChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — The settled order — a state, so it also fires on the first commit.

- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion nothing FLIPs and a promotion is an instant exchange, while the rule still drains and the counts still change, because how much is waiting is information.

### Underline Peek (KQ-1091) — `underline-peek`
The underline opens into the page.

A link whose underline opens into its preview: after a short rest the line drops away from the word as a ribbon its exact width on snap, then spreads into a card that hangs from a tab under the word, one outline rebuilt each frame with concave fillets where tab and card meet. Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/underline-peek`

Props:

- `rel`: string — Passed to the anchor.
- `onClick`: MouseEventHandler<HTMLAnchorElement> — The link's click, after the touch first-tap guard.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A soft swish as it unfurls and a paper fold as it closes, panned to the link.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The preview never opens; the link still works.
- `className`: string — Classes for the link itself.

Notes:

- Touch: the first tap opens the preview instead of navigating, the second tap follows the link, and a tap anywhere else folds it.

### Cross Grid (KQ-1093) — `cross-grid`

### Overflow Glide (KQ-1094) — `overflow-glide`
The rest of the line, when you ask.

A line cut to its box that, pointed at or tabbed to, glides left at reading speed until its last character reaches the edge, holds there, and eases home on the glide spring, which takes the pan's velocity, so a line let go mid-read slows, turns and returns. Speed is words per second, a word being five characters, and the ellipsis dissolves within its own width of travel while masked edges follow what is hidden on each side. It answers to the hover and keyboard focus of the link, button or row around it; on touch the first tap reads and the second acts.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/overflow-glide`

Props:
- `children`: string — The line. Cut to its box at rest; the rest glides into view when asked for.
- `speed`: number (default 3) — Reading pace in words per second, where a word is five characters, so a name with no spaces reads at the same pace as a sentence.
- `pause`: number (default 0.8) — Seconds held at the end of the line before it eases home.
- `fade`: boolean (default true) — Soft ramps at the cut edges, following how much text is hidden on each side, instead of hard edges.
- `loop`: boolean (default false) — Keep reading, again and again, while the line is pointed at or focused.

- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:
- Keyboard: tabbing to the host (a row button, a link) starts the glide on focus-visible and tabbing away sends it home. A cut line with no interactive host is itself a tab stop; a line that fits is never one, and never glides.
- The full text is always in the DOM and the ellipsis is aria-hidden, so assistive technology reads the whole name through the host; the glide is for eyes. On touch, the first tap on a cut line is stopped before the host's handler and reads it; the second tap acts.
- Under reduced motion the line does not travel: it pages through with fades, one window less 15% at a time, holding each page for its reading time at the same words per second, then fades home.
- The window is masked, never covered, so the line sits on any background, a hovered row included.

### Conjure Button (KQ-1098) — `conjure-button`
The words come apart, then come back finished.

A generate button whose own label is the material. Pressed, its letters lift off one after another and become glyph particles orbiting inside the pill on a glide spring while a band of light scans it; when the host's status says done, every particle condenses onto a letter of the new label on the same spring and a spark flares from the icon, and when it says error the orbit scatters and the pill shakes once on a tween. - `onConjure`: () => void | Promise<unknown> — The work. Uncontrolled, a returned promise settles the run (resolve for done, reject for error); a plain return means the work is already done.
- `label`: string — The label at rest, before a run, and the button's accessible name then.

- `shimmer`: boolean (default true) — Scan a band of light across the button while the host works.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the run's synthesised sounds: a shimmer and a rise on the lift, a chime on the spark, a thud on a failure. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:
- It is a native button: Space and Enter press it through the same path as a click. While the host works it is aria-busy and ignores presses but keeps focus, and a polite status announces the working, done or error label once the host has set it.

- The particles are DOM glyphs placed by motion values from one clock and four shared progresses, each mapped through a seeded delay, so nothing re-renders per frame, nothing is random, and the clock runs only while the swarm is alive.

- `onCancel`: (reason: "cancel" | "timeout" | "escape") => void — Fires when the question closes unanswered, with why.

- `split`: "crack" | "slide" (default "crack") — A zigzag crack that snaps apart, or a clean seam that glides.
- `tone`: "danger" | "neutral" (default "danger") — Destructive red, or the primary accent for confirms that are serious but not destructive.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the synthesised tink of the crack, the clack of the rejoin and the thock of the confirm. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:
- Every state is native buttons. Pressing the whole button moves focus to Confirm as it arrives; Left/Right (and Home/End) cross between the halves, Escape cancels and returns focus to the whole button, and a timeout returns focus only if it was inside. Confirm arms about 320ms after the split and ignores key repeat, so a double press or a held Enter cannot confirm by accident.
- Under reduced motion the gap appears at once, the halves cross-fade their colours and labels, and the rejoin is an instant close; the countdown hairline still shortens, because the time left is information. The sounds are unchanged.
- The halves open inside the control's own box (sized for its widest state), so neighbours never move. The countdown pauses while the page is hidden, and a polite status says what is being asked, then Timed out or Cancelled, then the confirmed label once the host holds it.

### Clicker Count (KQ-1100) — `clicker-count`
Every press, counted by hand.

A hand tally counter. Pressing the body sinks the plunger on a flick spring while the units wheel turns one notch on the same spring, then the plunger returns on a snap spring and the wheel stays; with carry on the wheels are geared, so 099 to 100 turns three wheels in one stroke. A long press on the reset knob turns it and winds every wheel back toward zero as the hold fills, and letting go early springs them home. Space and Enter count, and holding Space or Enter on the knob is the long press.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/clicker-count`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — Controlled or initial count. It rolls over past the last wheel, like the real thing.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the press or the finished reset, with the new count.
- `label`: string — What is being counted. Names the counter and its buttons, and is spoken with the count.
- `digits`: number (default 4) — Number wheels in the window, 3 to 5.
- `travel`: number (default 8) — How far the plunger sinks, in px: short and snappy, or long and heavy. The click pitches with it.
- `finish`: "steel" | "brass" | "matte" (default "steel") — The body's finish, built from theme tokens so it reads on a light or a dark stage.
- `carry`: boolean (default true) — Geared wheels: a rollover turns the next wheel in the same stroke and a reset rewinds through every number. Off, the wheels above the units turn freely to their own digits.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the synthesised click and clack of each press, a whir that rises while the knob is held, and the landing on zero. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the plunger and the knob.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:
- A group named by its label holds two native buttons. The body counts: Space and Enter make a full stroke with both sounds, and a held Enter keeps counting like a held plunger. The knob resets: hold Space or Enter for the same 800ms as a pointer (key repeat is ignored, Escape or blur lets go), and an assistive-technology click, which cannot hold, runs the full reset. A polite status speaks the count.
- Under reduced motion the plunger darkens instead of travelling, the digits swap in place, and the knob does not turn; its progress ring still fills while it is held and the wheels swap to zero when it completes. The sounds are unchanged.
- Controlled, the press and the finished hold report through onValueChange and the wheels turn when the host's value arrives; if the host refuses a reset, the knob lets go and the wheels run back to the count it still holds.

### Keycap Press (KQ-1101) — `keycap-press`
It goes down when you press the real key.

A mechanical keycap that is a real button: it goes down when it is clicked, when Space or Enter presses it, and when its own shortcut is typed anywhere on the page, and it stays down for as long as the key is held. The switch sets the stroke — a clicky cap holds at the jacket on a decelerating tween then slams to the floor on an underdamped spring that rattles off the bottom, a tactile cap hitches at a softer bump and lands composed, a linear cap falls in one smooth stroke — and every cap returns on the same stem spring carrying its release velocity. The legend lights at actuation, and the switch sounds on the frame the cap passes each point.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/keycap-press`

Props:
- `label`: string — The action, in a word or two: the key's accessible name, and the label legend.
- `shortcut`: string — The real key that presses it from anywhere on the page: "e", "shift+r", "mod+enter", "space", "/". mod is Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere.
- `onPress`: (via: "pointer" | "keyboard" | "shortcut") => void — Fires once per press, with what pressed it: on the click for pointer and keyboard presses, on keydown for the shortcut.
- `switch`: "clicky" | "tactile" | "linear" (default "clicky") — Sets the travel curve and the sound: a jacket that gives and slams with a click, a rounded bump and a thock, or one smooth stroke and a muted thud.
- `height`: number (default 8) — The cap's skirt height in px, 4 to 14. Travel is 0.7 of it, and a taller cap sounds deeper.
- `legend`: "both" | "key" | "label" (default "both") — What is printed on the cap: the key glyph over the label on a 1.5u cap, the key glyph alone on a 1u cap, or the label alone on a cap that widens to fit.
- `glow`: boolean (default true) — A backlight halo in the well around the cap, faint at rest and blooming with the legend on actuation.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the switch's synthesised sounds. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the key, blocks presses and stops listening for the shortcut.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the button's classes.

Notes:
- It is a native button named by its label, with aria-keyshortcuts: Space and Enter hold it down for as long as they are held and press it through the native click, a click from assistive technology plays a whole tap, and a held Enter does not repeat the action.
- The shortcut listens on the document but never takes a key the page already handled (defaultPrevented) or one typed into a field, a select or editable text; it claims the key when it acts, so a second key with the same shortcut does not also fire, and a key that is disabled, hidden, inert or behind an open dialog does not listen.
- Under reduced motion the cap swaps straight between up and down with no curve, and the legend, the halo and the sound still answer, because a press is information.
- Keep the label to a word or two: the cap is sized by its legend and does not wrap.

### Copy Slip (KQ-1102) — `copy-slip`
The text slips out and into the clipboard.

A copy field whose Copy button is a clipboard with its clip standing open. Pressed, a paper slip carrying the text lifts off the value and flies in a true throw — x linear, y a measured arc that never leaves the component — into the clipboard, where the clip clamps shut on snap and the glyph takes the landing on recoil; the button says Copied until the clip reopens. The slip only goes in if the clipboard took the text: a refusal bounces it back out on recoil, selects the text and says why in words, and Enter and Space copy through the same press.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/copy-slip`

Props:
- `value`: string — What is copied, and shown in the field.
- `label`: string — Names the field. The button is named by its word plus this: "Copy Payment link".
- `arc`: number (default 0.8) — How high the slip is lobbed, 0 to 1: 0 slides it straight along the row, 1 uses all the room above it. The swish rises with it.
- `slip`: number (default 0.5) — How light the paper is, 0 to 1: a stiff card thrown straight and fast, or a slip that hangs, leans along its path, flutters and takes its time.
- `hold`: number (default 2) — Seconds the clip stays shut and the button says Copied. The clock pauses while the page is hidden.
- `showText`: boolean (default true) — Print the copied text on the slip; off draws ruled lines, for values that should not fly past a shared screen.
- `onCopy`: (value: string) => void — Fires once the clipboard has taken the value.
- `onCopyError`: (reason: "insecure" | "blocked" | "unavailable") => void — Fires when the clipboard refused: an insecure page, a denied permission, or a writer that failed or did not answer.
- `writer`: (text: string) => Promise<void> — Writes the text. Defaults to the system clipboard's writeText; swap in rich copy or a test double.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the paper and the clip. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Disables the button and dims the field.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root element's classes.

Notes:
- The Copy button is a native button named by its visible word and the field's label ("Copy Payment link", then "Copied Payment link"); Enter and Space copy through the same press, and one polite status line says "Payment link copied." only after the clipboard has answered.
- A refusal is said in words, not colour alone: the button reads Failed, a line under the field names the reason (an insecure page, a blocked clipboard) and the value is selected so ⌘C or Ctrl+C copies it by hand; the line is measured and grows in, never reserved.
- Under reduced motion there is no flight and no clamp travel: the sheet appears in the clipboard and the clip shows shut, and the words, the hold and the sounds are unchanged.
- Presses during a flight are absorbed, since the same copy is already on its way; a press while the clip is shut starts the whole thing over, hold clock included.

### Pour Hold (KQ-1103) — `pour-hold`
Hold to pour; let go to stop.

A value input you fill by pouring: holding tips a carafe on a weighted spring, and once it passes the pour angle a stream leaves the mouth in a real ballistic arc, lands in the glass, and from that frame the level (the value) rises. Letting go rights the carafe, the stream's tail falls and lands as the last drop, and the surface rocks back to level on a spring whose damping is the liquid's viscosity, while the glass's own shape turns volume into height so a flute climbs fast and a jar slowly. It is a slider: arrow keys pour or lower one step, Page keys ten, End pours to the brim, Home empties, and Space or Enter held pours for as long as they are held.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pour-hold`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue`: number (default 0) — The amount poured, 0 to max. Controlled or uncontrolled; the level follows a pour as it happens and settles on whatever the host says once it ends.
- `onValueChange`: (value: number) => void — Fires from the pour or the key that changed it: once for each step a pour crosses, and once for each key step or empty.
- `max`: number (default 100) — What a full glass is worth.
- `step`: number (default 5) — The value's resolution, what one arrow key pours, and what a tap pours.
- `label`: string — What is being poured: the slider's accessible name, also shown over the reading.
- `format`: (value: number, max: number) => string — The reading under the glass and the slider's spoken value. Defaults to a percentage of max.
- `emptyLabel`: string (default "Empty") — The text of the button that empties the glass.
- `rate`: number (default 0.5) — How hard it pours, 0 to 1: the tilt, the stream's thickness, the flow (about 6 s to fill at 0, 1.6 s at 1) and the loudness.
- `viscosity`: number (default 0.2) — Water to syrup, 0 to 1: slower flow, a thicker and denser stream, a lower pour note, and a surface that barely sloshes.
- `glass`: "tumbler" | "flute" | "jar" (default "tumbler") — The glass's shape, which sets both the drawing and how fast the level climbs for the same pour.
- `overflow`: boolean (default false) — Let a held pour run over the brim: the surface domes, a sheet runs down the outside and pools, and the value stays at max. Off, the carafe rights itself at the brim and a further hold is refused.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the pour, whose pitch rises as the glass fills, and the last drop. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims the instrument, takes it out of the tab order and stops any pour.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes.

Notes:
- The instrument is a vertical role="slider" with aria-valuetext from format: ArrowUp/ArrowRight pour one step (held, they keep pouring), ArrowDown/ArrowLeft lower one, PageUp/PageDown move ten, End pours to the brim, Home empties, and Space or Enter held pours exactly like a held pointer, sounds included. The Empty button is a real button.
- Under reduced motion the carafe swaps poses with no swing, the stream appears and goes whole and the surface stays flat, while the level still rises for as long as you hold and stops when you let go, because the level is the value.
- A hold never selects text or opens the browser's menu, and a pour stops at once on pointer cancel, window blur or a hidden page. A tap pours one step.

### Peek Hold (KQ-1104) — `peek-hold`
Hold to look before you open.

A list whose rows you can look into before you open them: a long press charges while the rest of the list starts to blur, then the row lifts out of the page on the snap spring and grows into a floating preview on the glide spring, with its actions beside it. Without letting go, sliding onto an action highlights it on a snap-spring pill and releasing chooses it; releasing on nothing cancels, and the card glides back down into its row, while a still release leaves the preview open. - `delay`: number (default 450) — How long a press charges before the row lifts, in ms. The charge (the row sinking, the list blurring) runs exactly this long.
- `lift`: number (default 12) — How far the row rises as it comes free, in px; its scale and shadow grow with it, and 0 is a flat, in-place expansion.

### Fuse Button (KQ-1105) — `fuse-button`
The spark runs the edge; hold till it lands.

A hold-to-confirm button whose own border is a fuse: holding lights it at the top centre and a spark runs clockwise round the button's edge, leaving a charred thread with a short stretch still glowing behind it, while the face presses in on the flick spring. Letting go pauses it where it is, with the burnt part kept and the spark dimmed to a smouldering ember; completing the lap flares the whole edge, lands the face on the recoil spring and fires onConfirm, and Escape puts a lit fuse out as the char draws back on the glide spring. It is a native button: Space or Enter held burns it exactly as a held pointer does.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/fuse-button`

Props:

- `onStateChange`: (state: "idle" | "burning" | "paused" | "fired", progress: number) => void — Each change of state, with the share of the fuse burnt from 0 to 1. Never called per frame.
- `laps`: number (default 1) — How many times the spark goes round, 1 or 2. Two laps draw a second, inner strand and take twice as long.
- `burn`: number (default 2) — Seconds per lap.
- `spark`: number (default 0.6) — How fierce the spark is, 0 to 1: its glow and core, how many embers fly and how far, and how loud the sizzle and crackle are.
- `smoke`: boolean (default true) — Smoke curls up off the burning spark, behind the button's face.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the sizzle while it burns, its crackle, and the flare when it fires. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Dims and disables the button and pauses a burning fuse.
- `className`: string — Merged onto the root's classes (the button and the frame its sparks stay inside).

Notes:
- A native button described by a hold hint: Space or Enter held burns the fuse for as long as it is held (repeats ignored) and letting go pauses it; a click from assistive technology, whose user cannot hold, burns it through; Escape puts a lit or paused fuse out; and a polite live region speaks each change once (paused at a percentage, confirmed, fuse out).
- Under reduced motion the spark still runs the edge and the char still grows, because progress is the information, but there are no embers, no smoke, no smoulder and no pressed face, and the flare is a flash of colour.
- A hold never selects text or opens the browser's menu, the button is touch-none so a resting finger is not taken for a scroll, and pointer cancel, window blur or a hidden page pause the fuse and stop the sizzle. Once fired and released, the fuse is re-laid after a moment.

### Print Hold (KQ-1106) — `print-hold`
Hold your thumb; the ridges light.

A hold-to-confirm pad drawn as a procedural fingerprint that reads nothing and says so: held, its ridges light along a spiral that unwinds from the press point on a linear read while a hum rises; lifted early they drain back into the press point, and a thumb that slides smears the read, so the pad shakes on a keyframed tween, flashes and buzzes. - `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the rising scan hum, the chime on confirmation and the buzz on a failed read. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.
