### Mail Field (KQ-1170) — `mail-field`
Catches the typo before you do.

An email field that checks as you type and catches a slipped domain: when the domain looks finished but sits an edit or two from a known one (a swap counts as one), a row folds open under the field at its measured height on springs.glide, and using the fix morphs the address in place — kept letters slide on springs.glide, swapped letters trade places with one arcing over the other, a wrong letter drops out as the right one drops in on springs.snap, one after another on cascade(). A committed valid address is stamped with a postmark that lands on springs.recoil. The fix is the next thing Tab reaches, Enter or Space uses it, and Escape in the field declines it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mail-field`

Props:
- `label`: string — What the address is for. The field's visible label.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default "") — The address, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (value: string) => void — Fires from the key, paste or accepted fix that changed the address.
- `onStamp`: (value: string) => void — Fires when a valid address is stamped: the field was left, Enter pressed, or a fix used or declined.
- `suggest`: boolean (default true) — Offer a fix when the domain looks like a slip of a known one.
- `stamp`: boolean (default true) — Stamp a committed valid address; off, it gets a quiet check.
- `domains`: "common" | "work" (default "common") — Which built-in (invented) domains the field knows and suggests: personal mail hosts or company domains.
- `knownDomains`: string[] — The host's own known domains, in place of the built-in list.
- `name`: string — Form field name; the input itself carries the address.
- `placeholder`: string (default "name@fernmail.com") — Shown in an empty field.
- `hint`: string — Helper text under the field.
- `error`: string — An error from the host; replaces the hint and marks the field invalid.
- `required`: boolean (default false) — An empty field is invalid once it has been left.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Turns the field off.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the letters landing and the stamp. Only the visitor's own actions are heard.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root.

Notes:
- Keyboard: when a fix is offered, Tab from the field reaches "Use it" (then "Keep mine"); Enter or Space uses it and returns focus to the field with the caret at the end; Escape in the field declines it. Enter or leaving the field stamps a valid address.
- Reduced motion: no letters travel — the corrected address replaces the old one at once with its changed letters tinted and fading to ink, the suggestion row opens without travel, and the stamp fades in without the bounce.
- Certain mistakes (a space, a second @, a character an address cannot hold) are said at once; an unfinished address only once the field is left; the suggestion, errors and the stamp are each announced once in one polite live region.

### Ribbon Tabs (KQ-1171) — `ribbon-tabs`
Tabs that hang like ribbons.

Tabs drawn as lengths of fabric hanging from a rail: the chosen ribbon drops further on a spring set by the cloth and its colour deepens on a tween, while every ribbon is a pendulum that the change of tab tugs into a swing, the new one hardest, with a wave of smaller kicks running along the rail and each tail lagging so the cloth bends. The panel below cross-fades in the direction of travel and its height glides; brushing the pointer across the ribbons sets them swinging, and a ribbon pulled down like a cord follows the hand 1:1 and is chosen past half its drop. It is a real tablist: arrow keys move and choose with the same sway, Home and End jump.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ribbon-tabs`

Props:
- `tabs`: { id: string; label: string; content: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }[] — The ribbons, left to right, and what each one's panel shows.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first enabled tab) — The chosen tab's id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the tap, tug or key that chose a tab, with its id.
- `label`: string — The tab list's accessible name.
- `sway`: number (default 0.5) — How freely the ribbons swing, 0 to 1: 0 hangs rigid, 1 swings long and lazily.
- `fabric`: "satin" | "linen" | "velvet" (default "satin") — The cloth: glossy satin with a swallowtail, matte linen with a stitched hem, or heavy velvet with a pointed end. Sets the look, the cut and the weight of the swing.
- `length`: number (default 40) — How much further the chosen ribbon drops than the rest, in px (24 to 64).
- `color`: string (default "var(--accent)") — The fabric's colour, any CSS colour; the pale and deep shades are drawn from it at fixed lightness.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish when the visitor changes tab, and a soft one when a fast brush crosses a ribbon.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Every ribbon can be read but not chosen, tugged or brushed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which holds the rail and the panel.

Notes:
- A role="tablist" of role="tab" buttons with roving tabindex: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move and choose (wrapping, skipping disabled tabs), Home and End jump, Enter and Space choose the focused tab; the panel is a labelled, focusable role="tabpanel".
- Under reduced motion nothing swings, drops or brushes: the chosen ribbon's length switches at once and its colour still deepens on a short tween, and the panel cross-fades in place without sliding.
- Ribbons pull down with touch-action pan-x, so a vertical drag on them tugs rather than scrolls; a sideways brush never chooses a tab.

### Cabinet Menu (KQ-1172) — `cabinet-menu`
Drawers within drawers.

A nested menu drawn as a filing cabinet: each top item is a drawer that slides out toward you on its runners, the front coming down and growing a hair nearer while the inside is revealed above it with walls, runners and hanging folders, and at depth 3 a folder opens on the glide spring to fan out its sheets. The slide is one spring per drawer set by runners, from wooden slides that stop dead to ball-bearing slides that bump the end-stop and rebound when shut hard, with a thock timed to the stop; the pull follows the hand 1:1 and a throw is projected open or shut. It is a vertical menubar: Up and Down walk a level, Right, Enter or Space open and step in, and Left or Escape push the innermost drawer or folder home one at a time.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cabinet-menu`

Props:
- `drawers`: { id: string; label: string; folders: { id: string; label: string; items?: { id: string; label: string; meta?: string }[] }[] }[] — The cabinet, top drawer first: each drawer's folders and each folder's sheets.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default null) — The chosen leaf's id (a sheet, or a folder that is a leaf), controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string, path: string[]) => void — Fires from the press or key that chose a leaf, with its id and the labels from drawer to leaf.
- `onOpenChange`: (drawerId: string | null) => void — Fires when a drawer comes out, with its id, or when every drawer is home, with null.
- `label`: string — The menu's accessible name.
- `depth`: number (default 3) — How many levels the menu has: 2 (drawers, folders as leaves) or 3 (drawers, folders, sheets).
- `runners`: number (default 0.6) — The runners, 0 to 1: plain wooden slides that stop dead, up to ball-bearing slides that glide, bump the end-stop and rebound when shut hard. Also changes the runner hardware drawn.
- `finish`: "steel" | "oak" | "mint" (default "steel") — The cabinet's material: brushed steel with chrome pulls, oak with grain and brass pulls, or mint enamel.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a thock when a drawer the visitor moved meets its stop, and paper as folders open and a leaf is chosen.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The cabinet can be read but no drawer opens.
- `className`: string — Classes for the cabinet's carcass.

Notes:
- A vertical role="menubar" of drawer fronts (roving tabindex), each owning a role="menu" of folders; folders with sheets own a nested menu and leaves are menuitemradio with aria-checked. Up and Down walk a level, Home and End jump, a letter jumps ahead, Right, Enter or Space open and step in, Left or Escape push the innermost open level home one per press (Escape calls preventDefault whenever it closes something); a press outside or tabbing away shuts the cabinet.
- Under reduced motion nothing slides or bounces: a drawer's inside appears at full height with a short fade and a folder's sheets appear together; the chosen leaf is still marked and the drawer's label holder still names it.
- The bar pull is the only touch-action none area, so the rest of the cabinet still scrolls a page; the choice is announced once, politely.

### Cantilever Menu (KQ-1173) — `cantilever-menu`
Every tool, one lift away.

An actions menu drawn as a cantilever toolbox: opening lifts the trays up and outward on parallelogram arms, each tray staying level while it rides a true circular arc over the top and out into a staircase, and its tools stand up out of it as it clears the tray below. One spring per tray drives the arc, the arms and the tools; arms sets the linkage from one stiff unit to springy arms that stagger and bounce at their stops with a clack each, and closing folds the trays back from the bottom up until the latch clicks. Choosing a tool lifts it out on snap before the box shuts; arrow keys walk the tools and cross trays, Up and Down move between trays, and Escape hands focus back to the latch.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cantilever-menu`

Props:
- `groups`: { id: string; label: string; actions: { id: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; shortcut?: string; tone?: "default" | "danger" }[] }[] — One group per tray, top tray first, up to four actions each; groups beyond the trays share the box's own compartment.
- `label`: string — The menu's name: the latch's accessible name, shown on its plate while shut.
- `onAction`: (id: string) => void — A tool was chosen. Fires as it lifts out, before the box folds shut.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default false) — Whether the box is open, controlled or initial.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the press, pull or key that opened or shut the box.
- `trays`: number (default 3) — How many tiers of trays the box has, 1 to 3. With fewer tiers than groups, the rest sit in the box.
- `arms`: number (default 0.5) — How springy the linked arms are, 0 to 1: 0 moves the trays as one stout, stiff unit; 1 has slender arms that let each tray lag the one above and bounce at its stop.
- `finish`: "red" | "steel" | "green" (default "red") — The paint: red enamel, bare steel or green.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a clack as each tray the visitor opened reaches its stop and as a tool lifts out, and a click when the latch catches.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The box stays shut and the latch cannot be pressed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which is as tall as the box's tallest pose and scales down below 300 px wide.

Notes:
- The latch is a menu button (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls): Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it on the first tool and ArrowUp on the last. Inside the role="menu", ArrowLeft and ArrowRight walk the tools and cross trays, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move to the nearest tool in the tray above or below, Home and End jump, a letter jumps ahead, Enter or Space chooses, and Escape or Tab shut the box (with preventDefault) and return focus to the latch.
- Under reduced motion there are no arcs, bounces or rising tools: the trays fade out of the stack and into the staircase and back, the tools already standing; the highlight, the latch plate and the sounds still answer.
- The grip on top of the shut box pulls it open 1:1 (touch-action pan-x on the grip only) and a throw commits open or shut; while shut, the trays are inert and hidden from assistive technology.

### Thumb Index (KQ-1174) — `thumb-index`
Jump straight to the letter.

Section navigation cut into a book's fore-edge: half-moon notches run down the page's edge, each with a printed tab, and a drawn thumb rests in the current one. Pressing a tab lifts the thumb on flick, carries it down the edge on glide and drops it into the new notch on snap, whose one overshoot is the press; the tab stays down and the pages riffle to the section, leaves hinged at the spine turning over one after another on a single staggered clock while the running heads of the sections passed flick by. Arrow keys move between tabs, Home and End jump, a letter moves to the tab that holds it, Enter or Space presses, and the thumb can be dragged down the edge to scrub.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/thumb-index`

Props:
- `sections`: number | { id: string; label: string; title?: string; letters?: string; href?: string }[] (default 8) — How many sections to split A–Z into (4 to 12, balanced by how much of a dictionary each letter fills), or the sections themselves. A section with an href makes its tab a link.
- `value / defaultValue`: string — The current section's id. An id that is not found falls back to the section holding its first letter, so a letter id survives a change of section count.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the press, key or scrub that chose a section, with its id.
- `children`: (section: ThumbIndexSection, index: number) => ReactNode — What the page shows for a section, under its running head. Rendered again on the leaf that carries the page during a riffle.
- `label`: string (default "Sections") — The navigation's accessible name.
- `tabs`: "round" | "square" (default "round") — Half-moon notches with round tabs, or square-cut notches with square tabs.
- `riffle`: number (default 0.6) — How many leaves turn on the way to a section, and how slowly, 0 to 1. A longer jump turns more leaves; 0 changes the page with a fade.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a thock when the thumb lands in a notch and a paper riffle for the turning leaves, only in answer to the visitor.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The page can be read but the tabs cannot be pressed or scrubbed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which sets the page's size. Defaults to h-104 w-full; the notches spread down whatever height it is given.

Notes:
- A nav of links or buttons with aria-current="page" on the current section and a roving tabindex: ArrowUp and ArrowDown (or Left and Right) move between tabs, Home and End jump, a letter key moves focus to the tab whose section holds that letter, and Enter or Space presses it. The new section is said once in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion the thumb fades between notches instead of travelling and the page cross-fades instead of riffling; the pressed tab, the page and the announcement still change. Scrubbing still follows the finger.
- alphabetSections(count) is exported for hosts that want the same balanced A–Z split to filter their own content by each section's letters.

### Key Ring (KQ-1175) — `key-ring`
Pick the key for the workspace.

A workspace switcher drawn as keys hanging from a split ring, each bow capped in the workspace's colour and printed with its initial, each blade cut with teeth seeded from its id. Choosing turns the ring the short way on snap so the chosen key hangs at the front, a click ticking as each key passes; the keys are pendulums that trail the ring, swing and knock when it stops with a damping set by jingle, and a new workspace threads on at the split and slides round to its place on glide. The ring is a focusable listbox: arrow keys turn it and choose, Home and End go to the ends, a letter turns to the next workspace with that initial, and a horizontal drag spins it 1:1 and settles on the key the throw was heading for.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/key-ring`

Props:
- `workspaces`: { id: string; name: string; detail?: string; initial?: string; color?: string }[] — The workspaces, one key each. detail is the second line under the chosen name; color is any CSS colour for the bow, one of six pigments by default.
- `value / defaultValue`: string — The chosen workspace's id, whose key hangs at the front.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the key, click or drag that chose a workspace, with its id. A controlled ring that is refused turns back.
- `onAdd`: () => void — Shows an Add button at the ring's split end. A workspace the host then adds threads onto the ring there.
- `addLabel`: string (default "Add workspace") — The Add button's accessible name.
- `label`: string (default "Workspaces") — The listbox's accessible name.
- `keys`: number (default 5) — How many keys hang on the ring at once, 3 to 7. With more workspaces the ring turns through all of them, a key re-cut for the next one as it passes behind.
- `ring`: "steel" | "brass" | "black" (default "steel") — The metal of the ring and the blades, drawn as fixed pigments so both themes read the same.
- `jingle`: number (default 0.5) — How freely the keys swing and knock when the ring turns, 0 (stiff and silent) to 1.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a click as keys pass the front and when a key is threaded, and a clack when keys knock, only after the visitor's own turn.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The ring cannot be turned and Add is off.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root: a 272 px drawing over the chosen name.

Notes:
- A focusable listbox with one option per workspace and aria-activedescendant on the chosen one: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (or Up and Down) turn the ring one key and choose, Home and End go to the first and last workspace, and a letter turns to the next workspace with that initial. Pointer and drag choices are said once in a polite live region.
- Under reduced motion the ring does not turn and nothing swings: keys fade into their new places, a threaded key fades in where it hangs, and the chosen key is still the front one. A drag still turns the ring under the finger.
- The swing runs on a small frame loop only while the ring moves or a key still swings, and stops on a hidden page.

### Blind Menu (KQ-1176) — `blind-menu`
Opens slat by slat.

An account menu that hangs from its button like a window blind. Opened, the frame lowers to its length on glide while each slat, one item each, turns from nearly edge-on to face you on snap from the top down, stagger apart; the slat under the pointer or the focus leans toward you and catches the light, and closing draws the blind back up, slats turning shut from the bottom and rising into a stack under the headrail on exit tweens. It is the menu-button pattern: arrows move and wrap, Home and End jump, typing jumps to an item, Enter or Space chooses, and Escape closes and hands focus back to the trigger.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/blind-menu`

Props:
- `items`: { id: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; shortcut?: string; tone?: "default" | "danger"; disabled?: boolean }[] — The menu, one slat per item. A danger item is drawn in the danger colour; a disabled one is skipped by the arrows.
- `onSelect`: (id: string) => void — An item was chosen. Fires before the blind goes up.
- `label`: string — The account's name: the trigger's text and the menu's name.
- `detail`: string — A second line under the name: an email, a plan, a role.
- `avatar`: ReactNode — Before the name, 28 px. Defaults to the name's initials in a circle.
- `open / defaultOpen`: boolean (default false) — Whether the blind is down.
- `onOpenChange`: (open: boolean) => void — Fires from the press, key or outside press that opened or closed it.
- `slats`: number (default 5) — The most slats the blind lowers, 4 to 8. A longer menu scrolls inside it a slat at a time, with a mark on the bottom rail while there is more.
- `stagger`: number (default 0.5) — How far apart the slats turn open, 0 (all at once) to 1 (a slow wave), kept inside the 600 ms budget.
- `finish`: "wood" | "aluminium" | "fabric" (default "aluminium") — What the slats are made of: grained wood and curved aluminium are fixed pigments; fabric is woven from the menu's own surface colours.
- `align`: "start" | "end" (default "end") — Which edge of the trigger the blind hangs from.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish when the visitor lowers or raises the blind (pitched down going up) and a click when an item is chosen.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The trigger cannot be pressed.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which wraps the trigger; the blind hangs below it.

Notes:
- The trigger has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls; Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens with focus on the first item and ArrowUp on the last. Inside the menu of menuitems with a roving tabindex, arrows move and wrap, Home and End jump, typed letters jump, Enter or Space chooses, Escape closes with preventDefault and returns focus to the trigger, and Tab or a press outside closes it.
- Under reduced motion the blind fades in and out without lowering or turning, and a hovered or focused slat changes shade instead of leaning.
- Focus moves into the menu when its node arrives, and only when the visitor opened it: a host that opens it does not steal focus.

### Jukebox Menu (KQ-1177) — `jukebox-menu`
Pick a record.

A single-choice picker dressed as a jukebox: the catalogue sits on title strips in a book-style rack whose leaves turn about the spine on glide, riffling a leaf at a time across several pages, and every record has a letter-and-number code. A pick sends the changer arm round the fan of edge-on records on glide while its motor whirs, reaches in and grips the record, pulls it down to the spindle as it turns from edge-on to lying flat, and drops it on the platter on recoil before the tonearm swings on with snap. Under the chrome it is a listbox: arrows walk the strips and turn pages at the ends, Page keys turn a spread, a page letter and a strip number pick by code, and Enter picks the active strip.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/jukebox-menu`

Props:
- `records`: { id: string; title: string; artist?: string }[] — The catalogue, in rack order. Each record gets a code from its page letter and strip number.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | null (default null) — The id of the record on the turntable, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the strip, key or code that picked a record, with its id.
- `label`: string (default "Records") — The listbox's accessible name.
- `pages`: number (default 2) — How many pages the rack splits the catalogue across, 2 to 4; a page holds up to eight strips, and a longer catalogue adds pages.
- `finish`: "gold" | "silver" | "candy" (default "gold") — The cabinet's trim, rack frame and key tops, as pigments that read the same in both themes.
- `arm`: boolean (default true) — A changer arm fetches each record; off, the record rises from its slot and travels to the turntable by itself.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Clack for keys, strips and landings, and a whir while the arm travels. Only for the visitor's own picks and keys.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The rack and keys can be read but not used.
- `className`: string — Classes for the cabinet, which is w-full up to 360px.

Notes:
- The rack is a listbox with aria-activedescendant: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step through the strips and turn the page at either end, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight cross the spine, PageUp and PageDown turn a spread, Home and End jump, Enter or Space picks. Typing a page letter turns to that spread and waits; a digit then picks that strip. Escape clears a waiting letter. The selector keys are a toolbar with one tab stop.
- Under reduced motion nothing travels, turns or spins: the rack cross-fades between pages and the record appears on the platter, while the readout, the lit strip and the spoken 'Now playing' still change.
- Use jukeboxCodes(records, pages) to show the same codes elsewhere. The label turns only while the jukebox is on screen and the page is visible; a host changing value animates the arm silently.

### View Morph (KQ-1178) — `view-morph`
Grid, list, board — the items move themselves.

A collection with a switch for its layout: choosing Grid, List or Board re-lays every entry, and each one travels to its new place on the glide spring through motion's shared layout while its cover grows into a tile, shrinks to a thumbnail or thins to a colour strip, the details only one view has fading in and out and the measured height gliding with them. The switch is a radiogroup whose thumb slides on snap, and the chosen view's glyph starts as the view being left and morphs its six bars into its own shape on the same spring. Arrow keys move and choose a view, Home and End jump, and each entry is a button when onOpen is given.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/view-morph`

- `columns`: { id: string; label: string }[] — The board's columns, in order. Defaults to the statuses in order of appearance.
- `value / defaultValue`: "grid" | "list" | "board" (default "grid") — The view, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (view: "grid" | "list" | "board") => void — Fires from the press or key that chose a view.
- `label`: string (default "Collection") — The collection's heading and the name of its list and view switch.
- `stagger`: number (default 0.5) — How far apart the entries set off, 0 (all at once) to 1 (a ripple inside the 600ms budget).
- `items`: number — How many entries of the collection show; the header counts them against the whole. Defaults to all.
- `views`: 2 | 3 | "2" | "3" (default 3) — Offer grid and list, or grid, list and board.
- `maxHeight`: number — The most the collection grows to, in px; past it, it scrolls with a fade at the bottom edge.
- `onOpen`: (id: string) => void — An entry was opened. When given, every entry is a button named by its title, meta and status.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A click for the switch and a swish as the entries move, only when the visitor chose the view.

Notes:

A polite status says the new view and how many entries show.
- Under reduced motion the entries do not travel and the glyph does not morph: the collection fades up in its new layout and the height changes at once, while the chosen view and the announcement still change.

### Pocket Nav (KQ-1179) — `pocket-nav`
What doesn't fit tucks away.

A navigation bar that never wraps or scrolls: a ResizeObserver reads its room and every link's natural width, and the links that no longer fit slide along the bar into a pocket at its end on the exit ease, shrinking as they go, in priority order and a cascade apart, while the links behind them close the gap on glide. The pocket takes each one with a squeeze on snap as its count rolls, links slide back out on snap as room returns, and the current page is never tucked. The bar is one tab stop whose arrows move between links and the pocket; the pocket is a menu button whose menu of tucked links opens on ArrowDown, Enter or Space, moves with arrows, Home, End and first letters, and closes on Escape or Tab with focus back on the pocket.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pocket-nav`

Props:
- `links`: { id: string; label: string; href?: string; usage?: number }[] — The links, in bar order. With href a link is an anchor; usage ranks it for priority="usage".
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first link) — The current link's id, controlled or initial. It carries aria-current="page" and is never tucked.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the press, key or menu choice that made a link current.
- `onPocketChange`: (ids: string[]) => void — The links in the pocket, in bar order: once measured, then each time the set changes.
- `label`: string (default "Main") — The navigation's accessible name.
- `items`: number — The most links the bar shows at once, 4 to 9; the rest wait in the pocket even with room to spare. Defaults to all.
- `priority`: "order" | "usage" (default "order") — Tuck from the end of the bar backwards, or the least used links first wherever they sit.
- `pocket`: "more" | "dots" (default "more") — A More button with a count and chevron, or a round three-dot button with a count dot.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish for each link that slides into or out of the pocket and a tick as its count moves, only while the visitor is dragging or pressing keys; a swish when the pocket opens.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The links and the pocket can be read but not used.
- `className`: string — Classes for the nav, which fills its width.

Notes:
- The bar is one tab stop with a roving tabindex over its links and the pocket: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space follows a link. On the pocket, ArrowDown, Enter or Space open the menu on its first item and ArrowUp on its last; in the menu, arrows, Home, End and first letters move, Enter chooses, and Escape or Tab close it with preventDefault and hand focus back. A press outside closes it; a chosen link takes focus once it has arrived in the bar.
- Under reduced motion links fade out and in where they stand, the gap closes at once and the pocket does not squeeze, while its count and the announcement still change.
- Widths come from a clipped, zero-height measuring row, so late-loading fonts re-measure and nothing hidden adds scroll width. The first fit after measuring is instant and silent; when even the current link and the pocket cannot fit, the current link's label truncates.

### Liquid Tab Bar (KQ-1180) — `liquid-tabbar`
The indicator flows between tabs.

A bottom tab bar whose indicator is a drop of liquid behind the chosen icon: choosing a tab sends the drop's head racing there on a spring that keeps its velocity while the tail holds back on a softer, later spring, and the neck between them is drawn every frame as a metaball bridge that thins as it stretches and pinches off when stretched too far. The head squashes along its speed and lands with a jiggle whose size is set by the viscosity, and the icon it lands on bounces on recoil; the icons are drawn a second time in the tint's contrast colour, clipped to the drop's live shape. The drop can be dragged 1:1 and thrown to a tab, and the tablist's arrows move and choose, Home and End jump.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/liquid-tabbar`

Props:
- `items`: { id: string; label: string; icon: "home" | "search" | "inbox" | "chart" | "wallet" | "card" | "bell" | "calendar" | "person" }[] — The tabs, in order, each with a label and a built-in glyph.
- `value / defaultValue`: string (default the first item) — The chosen tab's id, controlled or initial.
- `onValueChange`: (id: string) => void — Fires from the tap, drag or key that chose a tab.
- `label`: string (default "Sections") — The tablist's accessible name.
- `panelId`: string — The id of the panel the tabs control, for aria-controls.

- `tint`: "accent" | "ink" | "signal" (default "accent") — The drop's colour and the contrast colour of the icon it covers; accent and signal are fixed pigments, ink follows the theme.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A blup when the drop lands on a tab the visitor chose, pitched by the tab and the viscosity.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The tabs and the drag cannot be used.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, which is w-full up to max-w-md.

Notes:
- It is a tablist with one tab stop: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move and choose (wrapping), Home and End jump, Enter and Space choose the focused tab. Dragging the drop along the bar follows the finger, rubber-bands past either end, and a release commits to the tab the throw was heading for; the bar uses touch-action pan-y so the page still scrolls.
- Under reduced motion the drop moves in one piece on a short tween with no neck, squash or bounce; the tint and the tinted icon still move, because which tab is chosen is the information.
- The drop is geometry, not a blur filter, so its edge stays crisp at any size; before the bar is measured (the server's render) a still drop sits on the chosen tab.

### Ink Bleed (KQ-1181) — `ink-bleed`
Words soak in, then dry.

A status line written in ink: each phrase soaks into the paper letter by letter on a seeded pen rhythm, landing as a drop on the baseline and wicking up through the glyph behind a feathered front, glossy while wet and drying to a lighter matte, and when it has rested a pad of blotting paper sweeps across and lifts it for the next phrase. - `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the pen, the drying, the rest and the blotter run, 0.5 to 2.
- `spread`: number (default 0.5) — How far the ink feathers into the paper, 0 (a crisp nib) to 1 (blotting paper): the soak front's softness, the halo, the drop and the smear.
- `paper`: "plain" | "laid" | "kraft" (default "laid") — The stock and how ink behaves on it: plain is coated and dries slowly with a long gloss, laid is cream with laid and chain lines, kraft is brown and thirsty — fast, matte and feathered.

- `onPhraseChange`: (index: number) => void — A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the paper is a button — Enter or Space runs the blotter along the line and blots every letter still wet, the same end state as dragging it across. A lift already under way completes first.
- Reduced motion: the whole phrase soaks in at once and keeps the reading time the pen would have given it, wet to dry is a colour change with no glint or drop, the lift is a fade and the keyboard blot dries the line in place; the dragged pad still follows the pointer and still lightens what it blots.
- The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase; the clock runs only while the paper is on screen in a visible page.

A status line printed by a platen press: a small head rides a rail over a strip of card stock, and for each letter its plunger falls with the letter, which squashes onto its baseline and springs back on springs.snap while the carriage steps on a stiff spring, every impression a little uneven in density, tilt and inking. The strip is a real button — a press, a tap, Enter or Space strikes the next letter by hand, and on a finished line sends the carriage home — and each phrase is announced once.

A status line written in sand on a canvas: a thin stream pours along the line and its grains fall and land in the letter shapes, the lowest first, so each letter heaps up in relief; when the phrase has rested, a wave runs up the beach with a foam lace, loosens every grain it reaches and drains back, leaving wet sand that dries as the next phrase pours. ### Morse Status (KQ-1187) — `morse-status`
Tapped out, then spelled.

A status line that is tapped out in Morse before it is spelled: a signal lamp sends each word with real ratios, and a head travelling the track under the line draws every dot and dash as long as the lamp was lit, so a dash is three dots long because it was on three times as long. When a word is complete each letter's marks lift off the track and condense into the printed letter on the glide spring while the letter resolves out of them, and the head glides on to the next word. The telegraph key is a real button whose lever dips on flick and springs back on snap; a tap, or Space or Enter, adds the visitor's own dot to the line and a hold draws a dash.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/morse-status`

- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the code is sent, 0.5 to 2: one unit is 50ms at 1, and the hold and fades scale with it.
- `lamp`: boolean (default true) — Show the signal lamp, which flashes with the code and lights the mark being drawn. Off, the head and the marks carry the signal alone.
- `trail`: number (default 0.6) — How long the marks stay lit on the track, 0 (each fades to a ghost within a moment) to 1 (every mark stays until its word is spelled); also the length of the light streak behind the head.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the key under the visitor's hand: a click as the contact closes and a tick as the lever returns. The automatic sending is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The line keeps sending, but the key cannot be pressed.
- `onPhraseChange`: (index: number) => void — A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.
- `onWordChange`: (word: number) => void — A word of the phrase began to be sent: its index within the phrase. Also reported on the first commit.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the telegraph key is a button — Space or Enter held closes the line for as long as it is held (a dash), tapped sends a dot, exactly as the pointer does; a click from assistive technology sends one dot.
- Reduced motion: the lamp glows steadily instead of flashing, each letter's code appears whole on the track in the same rhythm, and a spelled word cross-fades in rather than condensing out of its marks; the key's lever does not travel.
- The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase, never per word or mark; the clock runs only while the line is on screen in a visible page.

### Kiln Glow (KQ-1189) — `kiln-glow`
Fired until it's done.

A determinate text loader fired like a glaze: the phrase stands in a kiln's spy window and its heat is the progress, climbing from dark iron through dull red, cherry, orange and yellow to white, each letter following on the drift spring with its own thermal mass so the heat arrives unevenly, while the letters light their own air, the back wall glows and a band of heat haze wavers above the words. At done the kiln goes out and the letters cool back down through the same colours to the glaze's fired colour, and every loop stops. A quick sweep of the pointer across the window cools the letters it passes for a moment, deeper the faster it goes, with a wisp of steam from the hot ones; the window is a button, and Space or Enter sweeps across every letter.

- `doneText`: string — What stays, fired, once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.
- `progress`: number — Determinate, 0 to 1: the letters' heat follows it, phrase i owns the band [i/n, (i+1)/n) and arrives at the current heat, and at 1 the kiln soaks for a moment and cools to the glaze.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the letters take and lose heat, the self-firing cycle and the haze's pace, 0.5 to 2.
- `heat`: number (default 0.8) — How hot the kiln gets at full progress, 0 (a dull red) to 1 (white heat), and with it the glow's reach, the wall's light and the haze.
- `glaze`: "iron" | "copper" | "ash" (default "copper") — The colour the letters cool to once fired, as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the quench under the visitor's sweep: a sizzle while hot letters are cooled and a snap of thermal shock for the hottest. Firing and cooling are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The kiln keeps firing, but the letters cannot be cooled by hand or by key.
- `onPhraseChange`: (index: number) => void — A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

- Reduced motion: no haze, steam or springs; the letters' colours still follow the heat on short tweens and a self-firing phrase still takes its time, because the heat is the progress, and a quench still darkens the letters and lets them warm back.
- The kiln's chamber is fixed dark art in both themes; the phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root, announced once, and the haze runs only while the kiln is warm, on screen and in a visible page.

### Lens Sweep (KQ-1190) — `lens-sweep`
Reading it over.

A status line read over by a loupe: outside the lens the words are soft and faint, under it they are sharp, full ink and magnified about the lens's centre. The lens reads in saccades, gliding from word to word on the glide spring from rest to rest and pausing on each as if checking it, with a small nod and a hairline check drawn under the word that stays as it moves on; a read phrase rests, fades, and the lens sweeps back for the next. The lens follows a finger 1:1 anywhere along the line, ticking as it enters each word, and on release settles onto the word the throw was heading for and reads on from there; a tap on a word sends it there, and as a slider Left, Right, Home and End move it a word at a time.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/lens-sweep`

Props:
- `phrases`: string[] — The status phrases, read over one after another and cycled in order.
- `active`: boolean (default true) — Reading. False puts the lens down beside the line and leaves doneText sharp, full ink and still; every timer stops.
- `doneText`: string — What stays, read, once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How long the lens checks each word and rests on a read phrase, 0.5 to 2; the glide itself stays the house glide.
- `zoom`: number (default 1.5) — How much the lens magnifies, 1.2 to 2.
- `blur`: number (default 1.5) — How soft the words outside the lens are, 0 to 4 px.
- `lens`: "round" | "bar" (default "round") — A jeweller's loupe, or a reading bar that magnifies a wider span of the line.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the lens under the visitor's hand: a tick for each word it enters while dragged, tapped to or moved by key, pitched along the line. The automatic reading is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The lens keeps reading, but it cannot be moved by hand or by key.
- `onPhraseChange`: (index: number) => void — A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.
- `onWordChange`: (word: number) => void — The lens came to rest on a word and checked it: its index in the phrase.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the lens is a slider over the words — Left and Right move it a word, Home and End to the ends, the same end state as putting it down there by hand; its value text names the word, and reading waits a second after each key before going on from there.
- Reduced motion: the lens does not glide — it appears at each word in turn with a short fade and the check appears whole; dragging is still 1:1 and a drop places it on the word directly.
- Two copies of the line share one layout: a still, blurred page copy, and a copy clipped to the lens, scaled from its corner and shifted by the centre times one minus the zoom, so the point under the lens stays put. The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root, announced once, and reading runs only on screen in a visible page.

An inline loader drawn as a small hourglass: sand runs from the top bulb onto a growing pile as a falling thread, conserved as drawn area so the top's level races where the bulb narrows, and when the top is empty the glass rests a beat and turns itself over on the snap spring while the sand rides the turn and slumps onto the neck. ### Abacus Count (KQ-1194) — `abacus-count`
Beads slide as the work counts up.

An inline loader drawn as a small counting frame: ten beads on each wire, the highest place on the left, one motion value per bead. The work counts up a bead at a time — each rises to the beam on the spring its material calls for (wood on springs.snap, glass on springs.recoil, stone on springs.glide) — and at ten the wire clears in a rattle while a bead rises on the next wire, so a determinate count (rows of a total, or percent) reads as beads and big jumps glide on springs.glide; without progress it counts to a seeded number and clears. The frame is a button: drag up and the next units bead follows the finger 1:1, a release past halfway flicks it home with the throw's velocity, and a tap, Enter, Space or the Up arrow does the same — free-running the flick adds one, determinate the bead is only lent and slides home if the work has not reached it.

Props:

- `hideLabel`: boolean (default false) — Keep the label for assistive technology only, for a glyph inline in a sentence or a row.

- `beads`: "wood" | "glass" | "stone" (default "wood") — What the beads are made of: how they look and how they land — wood snaps with one overshoot, glass rings in two bounces, stone lands dead.
- `progress`: number — Determinate, 0 to 1: the frame shows round(progress × min(total, 10^rods)) in beads, stepping bead by bead for small moves and gliding for big ones. Without it the frame counts and clears on its own.

The label sits beside it as role="progressbar" (with the percent and a value text) when progress is given, otherwise as a polite role="status"; it is a sibling of the button because a progressbar's children are presentational.
- Reduced motion: beads swap into place instead of sliding and carries clear at once, but the count still steps (at a third of the pace) and determinate counts still update, because the count is the information; a drag still moves the bead under the finger and settles at once.

- `size`: number (default 24) — The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64. Below 24 at most three blobs and no halo; below 44 no shine, glass highlight or base band.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the wax heats, rises, cools and sinks (a cycle of about seven seconds at 1), 0.5 to 2.
- `progress`: number — The share of the wax that has risen, 0 to 1; the label becomes a progressbar. The pool drains, a cap gathers under the top and blobs ride up between them; at 1 the lamp goes still. Omitted, the blobs rise and fall on their own.
- `wax`: "amber" | "rose" | "teal" (default "amber") — The wax and the liquid it floats in — amber in red, rose in violet, teal in blue — as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.
- `blobs`: number (default 4) — How many blobs rise and fall, 2 to 6; with progress, how many ride up at once.
- `glow`: number (default 0.6) — How much the lamp glows, 0 to 1: the halo round the glass, the bulb's light up the liquid and the shine on the wax.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The lamp keeps flowing but cannot be warmed by the pointer or a press.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, an inline-flex row of the lamp and its label.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the lamp is a button — Space or Enter warms the blob sitting on the bulb (or hurries the lowest rising blob while it fills), the same heat the pointer gives the blob nearest it.
- Reduced motion: the wax does not travel — it is drawn still, the glow breathes while the lamp works, the pool and cap still follow the progress at once, and a warm brightens the glow instead of moving wax.
- No sound. The label lives in a role="progressbar" (aria-valuenow 0–100) or a role="status"; the frame loop runs only on screen in a visible page and stops once a filled lamp is still.

### Sundial (KQ-1200) — `sundial-hour`
The shadow walks the hours.

An inline loader drawn as a garden sundial seen from above. The time of day — the progress, or a looping day — sets the gnomon's shadow by the real horizontal-dial formula, so hour lines crowd towards noon, and the sun's altitude sets its length: long and faint at morning and evening, short and dark at noon; a small sun rides the rim opposite, lighting that side of the plate, and the light warms from a cool dawn to a gold evening before a short dusk. With progress the time follows it on the drift spring and rests in the evening at 1. Dragging on the dial walks the shadow — a flick swing to the finger, then 1:1, ticking at every hour line it crosses — and letting go drifts it back to the real hour, or lets the looping day carry on from there; Left and Right walk it an hour at a time on glide.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sundial-hour`

Props:
- `label`: string (default "Loading") — What is waiting on the day: the loader's accessible name, shown beside the dial unless hideLabel.
- `hideLabel`: boolean (default false) — Keep the label for assistive technology only.
- `size`: number (default 24) — The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64. Below 24 only the plate, fin, shadow and sun; below 44 plain hour lines with no numerals, ticks or penumbra.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the looping day passes (about eight seconds and a short dusk at 1), 0.5 to 2.
- `progress`: number — How far through the day, 0 (06:00) to 1 (18:00); the label becomes a progressbar and the dial rests in the evening light at 1. Omitted, a day passes on a loop.
- `dial`: "stone" | "brass" | "slate" (default "stone") — The plate: weathered stone, polished brass or dark slate with light engraving, as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.
- `numerals`: "roman" | "arabic" | "ticks" (default "roman") — How the quarters are marked round the rim at 44 px and up: VI IX XII III VI, 6 9 12 3 6, or longer ticks.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A tick for every hour line the shadow crosses while the visitor walks it, bright in the morning and low in the evening, loudest at noon. The running day is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The day keeps passing but the shadow cannot be walked.
- `className`: string — Classes for the root, an inline-flex row of the dial and its label.

Notes:
- Keyboard: the dial is a button — Left/Right (or Down/Up) walk the shadow an hour, Page Up and Page Down three, Home and End to morning and evening, held keys keep walking and key up lets go, as releasing a drag does; Space or Enter walks it one hour on. With progress the shadow then drifts back to the real hour after a beat.
- Reduced motion: the shadow never sweeps — the looping day steps it hour by hour and dusk is a fade, a determinate dial jumps to the hour, and walking it still follows the hand and the keys and returns at once.
- The label lives in a role="progressbar" (aria-valuenow 0–100) or a role="status"; the looping day's frame loop runs only on screen in a visible page and pauses while a hand holds the shadow.

### Darkroom (KQ-1201) — `darkroom-develop`
Developing in the tray.

An image placeholder that develops the real picture like a print in a darkroom tray: under a red safelight it comes up from blank paper through a print's tone curve — shadows, then midtones, then highlights — in twelve bands, each sped where the developer's slosh has just washed over it. Dragging tips the tray 1:1 and the liquid, an underdamped oscillator drawn as a travelling crest and the lamp's glint, sloshes after it, so a hard rock brings the print up in half the time; the tray levels on springs.glide with the throw, keyboard rocks go out on springs.snap and home on springs.glide, and when the picture is ready the liquid drains, the safelight switches off and the room light brings up its colour. Arrow keys tip the tray and Enter or Space rocks it both ways.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/darkroom-develop`

Props:
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows. Exposed the whole time, while it develops and after.
- `src`: string — The image to develop. Without it, children is the picture.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The finished picture when there is no src: any element that fills its box, such as an inline SVG illustration.
- `ready`: boolean — Controlled readiness. Uncontrolled, an image is ready once it has loaded (or failed), and children at once — the print's own development is then the minimum run.
- `progress`: number — How much of the picture has arrived, 0 to 1. Until ready, the print holds at that stage.
- `onReady`: () => void — Fires once per print, when the lights are on and the picture is whole.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the print comes up and the hand rocks the tray, 0.5 to 2.
- `safelight`: boolean (default true) — Develop under a red safelight that switches off when the print is done. Off, it develops grey on white in plain light.
- `grain`: number (default 0.4) — Silver grain that clumps as the image forms and clears with the room light, 0 (clean) to 1 (coarse).
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish for each stroke of a rock, each keyboard rock and a flicked release. Development and the switch-off are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The print still develops; the tray cannot be rocked.
- `className`: string — Sizes the box; it is aspect-[4/3] w-full by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: while developing, the print carries a Rock the tray button — ArrowLeft and ArrowRight tip the tray that way and back, Enter or Space rocks it both ways, through the same liquid as a drag, so the print comes up faster either way. When it is done the button leaves and focus moves to the picture.
- Reduced motion: nothing travels — no rocking, wave or moving glint. The print still comes up, evenly, as a fade of tone and contrast; rocking by pointer or key still speeds it and brightens the sheen; the lights come on as a fade.
- The root is aria-busy until the picture is whole and the picture keeps its alt throughout. The clock runs only while developing, on screen, in a visible page; with src it also waits for the image to arrive before developing past a faint fog.

### Instant Shake (KQ-1202) — `instant-shake`
Shake it and it comes up faster.

An image placeholder presented as an instant photo: it feeds out of the camera's slot at a motor's steady pace and comes up in the hand, the real picture rising through a blue-grey or brown-amber murk that thins in mottled patches while brightness, contrast and colour return. Grabbing it swings it from the slot 1:1 like a pendulum, and every reversal is a stroke that agitates the chemistry so a hard shake brings it up in about half the time; let go, it swings home on springs.recoil with the throw, and when it is done the caption is written into the chin and the rollers let it drop onto springs.recoil. Arrow keys swing it, Enter or Space shakes it three times, ArrowDown pulls a feeding photo out.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/instant-shake`

Props:
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows. Exposed the whole time, while it develops and after.

- `children`: React.ReactNode — The finished picture when there is no src: any element that fills its box, such as an inline SVG illustration.
- `caption`: string — Written into the frame's chin, left to right, when the photo is done.
- `ready`: boolean — Controlled readiness. Uncontrolled, an image is ready once it has loaded (or failed), and children at once — the photo's own chemistry is then the minimum run.
- `progress`: number — How much of the picture has arrived, 0 to 1. Until ready, the chemistry holds exactly at that stage however hard it is shaken.
- `onReady`: () => void — Fires once per photo, when it has come up and let go of the camera.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the photo feeds out and the chemistry runs, 0.5 to 2.
- `tint`: "cool" | "warm" (default "cool") — The film's murk and colour cast while it develops: blue-grey clearing through cyan, or brown-amber clearing through amber.
- `frame`: "classic" | "wide" (default "classic") — The format: a square window with a deep chin, or a landscape window. The whole photo reshapes.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play a swish for each shake stroke and the motor's whir while a feeding photo is pulled out. The automatic feed and the chemistry are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The photo still feeds out and develops; it cannot be shaken or pulled.
- `className`: string — Sizes the instrument's width; it is w-full max-w-72 by default and its height follows the format.

Notes:
- Keyboard: while developing, the photo carries a Shake the photo button — ArrowLeft and ArrowRight swing it (one stroke each), Enter or Space shakes it three times, ArrowDown pulls a still-feeding photo out; each reaches the same faster chemistry as the pointer. When it is done the button leaves and focus moves to the picture.
- Reduced motion: nothing feeds, swings or drops — the photo fades in where it hangs, shakes by pointer or key still count and still speed the chemistry, the murk still clears, and the caption and the camera's departure are fades.

### Sketch to Paint (KQ-1203) — `sketch-paint`
Pencil first, then paint.

An image placeholder that paints the real picture in: a pencil sketch of its own edges (a Sobel edge filter broken by the paper's tooth, hatched in the shadows) is drawn in by one diagonal pass, then watercolour washes — the picture wobbled, softened, posterised and lifted toward the paper — bloom into it region by region in a painter's order, each bloom spreading fast and slowing as it dries to a tide line, and finally the picture resolves through the paint on the enter ease. The pointer is a wet brush: moving a mouse over the paper, or dragging a finger or pen, soaks the wash through under it at once and opens each region's bloom from the brush's own point, pulling the whole schedule forward. Enter or Space runs the brush along the next unpainted row.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/sketch-paint`

Props:
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows. Exposed the whole time, while it is painted and after.
- `src`: string — The image to paint. Without it, children is the picture.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The finished picture when there is no src: any element that fills its box, such as an inline SVG illustration.
- `ready`: boolean — Controlled readiness. Uncontrolled, an image is ready once it has loaded (or failed), and children at once — the painting itself is then the minimum run.
- `progress`: number — How much of the picture has arrived, 0 to 1. Until ready, the painting holds at that stage; the brush can still paint ahead of it.
- `onReady`: () => void — Fires once per painting, when the picture has resolved through the paint.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the sketch, the blooms and the drying run, 0.5 to 2.
- `wash`: number (default 0.5) — How wet the paper is, 0 to 1: tight, precise washes with crisp edges, or loose washes whose soft, wandering blooms overrun their regions and the pencil.
- `pencil`: "hb" | "4b" (default "hb") — The lead: a fine light HB line with sparse hatching, or a soft dark 4B with heavy hatching in the shadows.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — Play the bristles on the paper, pitched and as loud as the brush is fast, while the visitor paints, and during the keyboard's stroke. The painting itself is silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — It still paints itself; the brush does nothing.
- `className`: string — Sizes the box; it is aspect-[4/3] w-full by default.

Notes:
- Keyboard: while painting, the paper carries a Paint ahead button — Enter or Space runs the brush along the next row still unpainted, with the same marks, blooms and sound as the pointer, and pulls the schedule forward the same way. When it is done the button leaves and focus moves to the picture.
- Reduced motion: nothing sweeps or spreads — the sketch fades in, each region's wash fades in at its full shape when its turn comes, brush marks appear in place, and the picture cross-fades in; the brush ring still follows the pointer and painting ahead still hurries it.
- The root is aria-busy until the picture has resolved and the picture keeps its alt throughout; the sketch and wash copies are aria-hidden and inert. The clock runs only while painting, on screen, in a visible page, and the filtered copies sit on their own layers so only the paper cover is redrawn as the washes bloom.

### Screen Print (KQ-1204) — `screen-print`
Four pulls of the squeegee.

A picture that arrives as a screen print: a squeegee sweeps each ink layer across the sheet, laying it down behind its blade, each colour landing a few pixels off register, and when the picture is ready the last pull snaps every layer home on the snap spring before the print gives way to the picture. The sheet is also the grip — a drag pulls the blade 1:1 and a release finishes the pull on the glide spring with the throw's velocity. Enter or Space on the focused sheet pulls one layer.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/screen-print`

Props:
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows. On the picture from the first frame, loading or not.
- `src`: string — An image to load. Without it, children is the picture.
- `children`: React.ReactNode — The finished picture when there is no src: an illustration, a figure.
- `ready`: boolean — Controlled readiness. Uncontrolled, an image is ready once it has loaded (or failed), and children once every pull but the last has run.
- `progress`: number — How far the load has got, 0 to 1. The pulls follow it; the last one still waits for ready.
- `onReady`: () => void — Fires once per load, when the print has resolved into the picture.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — The pace of every pull, return and flood stroke, 0.5 to 2.
- `register`: number (default 2) — How far off register each ink lands, in px, 0 to 4. At 0 every pull is a clean proof.
- `inks`: "cmyk" | "riso" | "duo" (default "cmyk") — Four process inks, three risograph inks, or a two-ink duotone.
- `sound`: boolean (default false) — A swish for the visitor's own pulls. The automatic pulls are silent.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — The print still runs; the squeegee cannot be taken.
- `className`: string — Sizes the sheet. Defaults to w-full aspect-[3/2].

Notes:
- The sheet is a button while printing, named for the next ink: Enter or Space pulls one layer, a drag pulls by hand, and each visitor pull is announced politely ("Magenta pulled, 2 of 4."). When the print resolves, focus that was on it moves to the picture.
- Under reduced motion each pull is a cross-fade at the same pace, the squeegee rests at the edge, and the inks come into register in one frame before the print cross-fades to the picture.
- The separations are CSS filters over copies of the picture, so any children or src works; the root carries aria-busy until the picture shows, and the picture keeps its alt throughout.

### Kaleido Resolve (KQ-1205) — `kaleido-resolve`
Pieces turn until they fit.

A picture that loads as a kaleidoscope of its own wedges: one slice is turned into the even pieces and reflected into the odd, so every seam meets, and it keeps turning behind the mirrors while the picture loads. When the picture is ready the pieces open one by one clockwise on the snap spring — even pieces turn back upright, odd ones flip over on their hinges — until the plain picture remains. Circling the pointer turns it 1:1 and a throw carries on along the drift spring; it is a slider, so arrow keys turn it a step, Page keys a whole piece and Home turns it back.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/kaleido-resolve`

Props:
- `alt`: string — What the picture shows. On the picture from the first frame, loading or not.

- `ready`: boolean — Controlled readiness. Uncontrolled, an image is ready once it has loaded (or failed), and children after 1.6 s of on-screen turning.
- `progress`: number — How far the load has got, 0 to 1: that share of the pieces turns into place. The last piece waits for ready.
- `onReady`: () => void — Fires once per load, when the last piece has landed.
- `speed`: number (default 1) — The pace of the turning and of the pieces opening, 0.5 to 2.
- `wedges`: number (default 8) — How many mirrored pieces the kaleidoscope is cut into: 6, 8, 10 or 12 (rounded to an even count).

- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — It still resolves; it cannot be turned.
- `className`: string — Sizes the box. Defaults to w-full aspect-[3/2]; the box is a size container, so give it a definite size.

Notes:
- While loading, the kaleidoscope is a role="slider" named "Turn the kaleidoscope": arrow keys turn it 15°, Page keys one piece, Home back to 0, a drag circling the centre turns it 1:1. It leaves when the picture resolves; focus on it moves to the picture, and "Picture in place." is announced.
- Under reduced motion the mandala holds still (a hand still re-aims it directly) and the pieces fade away clockwise instead of turning, revealing the picture beneath.
- Each piece is a clipped, transformed copy of the picture, so any children or src works; the root carries aria-busy until the picture shows, and the picture keeps its alt throughout.

- `speed`: number (default 1) — How fast the pieces arrive and are put together, 0.5 to 2.
